SEHEMU YA 10 (Malkia wa Majini na Siri ya Nahodha)
​Giza lilizidi kuwa zito, na ule mwanga mweupe nilioutoa ulianza kufifia, ukimezwa na giza la kijani la Mfalme Maridadi. Zuwena alikuwa juu yangu, kucha zake zikinitoa alama za damu kooni kwangu. Lakini kabla hajanimaliza, sauti moja ya kike, yenye mamlaka na baridi kama barafu, ilisikika ikivuma kutoka kwenye kuta za pango.
​"Zuwena! Mwache huyo mwanadamu!"
​Zuwena alistuka na kurudi nyuma, akitetemeka. Kutoka kwenye giza la upande wa pili wa kiti cha enzi, kulitokea mwanamke mwingine. Alikuwa mrefu kuliko Zuwena, amevaa vazi lililotengenezwa kwa ngozi ya nyoka wa baharini na taji ya almasi za bluu. Huyu alikuwa Malkia Bi. Subira, mama yake Zuwena na mke wa kwanza wa Mfalme Maridadi.
​Tofauti na Mfalme, Malkia Bi. Subira alikuwa na sura ya kibinadamu kabisa, lakini macho yake yalikuwa na huzuni ya miaka elfu moja. Alinitazama, kisha akamtazama Mzee Zubery aliyekuwa anatoa roho.
​"Mume wangu," Bi. Subira alimgeukia Mfalme Maridadi. "Ulisema unamleta Shafih hapa ili awe mlinzi, siyo kafara. Unavunja sheria za kale za majini. Damu ya binadamu aliyeingia kwenye agano kwa upendo haitakiwi kumwagwa ndani ya mji huu."
​"Upendo?" Mfalme Maridadi alicheka kwa dharau, sauti yake ikipasua baadhi ya mafuvu ya dhahabu. "Shafih hakumpenda binti yetu, alipenda uzuri tuliojifunika! Sasa nataka 'Moyo wa Bahari' uliojificha ndani ya kovu lake ili niweze kupumua nchi kavu na kuangamiza kizazi chao chote!"
​Malkia Bi. Subira alinikaribia. Nilihisi harufu ya udi, lakini safari hii ilikuwa safi, haina uozo. Alishika mkono wangu wenye magamba na kovu. "Shafih, unajua kwa nini Nahodha alikusaidia? Unajua kwa nini alijitolea maisha yake kukuleta huku?"
​Nilitazama ule mwili wa Nahodha uliokuwa umelala sakafuni, hauna pumzi. "Alikuwa rafiki yangu..." nilisema kwa sauti ya kukwaruza.
​"Hapana," Malkia alinong'ona. "Nahodha ni kaka yake Zuwena. Ni mtoto wangu wa kwanza aliyepotea miaka mingi iliyopita baada ya kukataa amri ya baba yake ya kuua wanadamu. Alijigeuza binadamu na kuishi kijijini kwenu akisubiri siku ambayo 'Moyo wa Bahari' utazaliwa ndani ya mwanadamu... ili auokoe ufalme huu dhidi ya baba yake."
​Papo hapo, mwili wa Nahodha ulianza kutingishika. Lile gereza la mwani mwekundu lilipasuka kwa nguvu ya ajabu. Nahodha alisimama, lakini hakuwa Nahodha yule mzee niliyemjua. Alikuwa kijana shujaa, mwenye macho yanayowaka moto wa bluu, na mikononi mwake alishika mkuki uliotengenezwa kwa mfupa wa jini mkuu.
​"Imetosha, Baba!" Nahodha (au Pua la Jini, jina lake la asili) alinguruma. "Shafih siyo daraja la wewe kupita kwenda kuua watu! Yeye ndiye mwisho wa utawala wako wa damu!"
​Mfalme Maridadi, kwa hasira, alijibadilisha na kuwa joka kubwa la bahari lenye vichwa vitatu. Alimvamia Nahodha, na pambano likaanza. Kila mkuki wa Nahodha ulipopiga kuta za pango, tetemeko kubwa lilitokea, likisababisha mji wa dhahabu kuanza kuporomoka.
​"Shafih, chukua hili!" Malkia Bi. Subira alinikabidhi kisu kidogo cha matumbawe. "Ili kumuokoa baba yako, lazima uchome kile kovu lako mwenyewe. Ukifanya hivyo, utatoa nguvu ya 'Moyo wa Bahari'. Lakini tahadhari... ukifanya hivyo, hutakuwa binadamu tena, na wala hutakuwa jini. Utakuwa kiumbe wa kati na kati, mlinzi wa milele wa mipaka ya bahari na nchi."
​Nilitazama upande mmoja: Nahodha alikuwa anazidiwa nguvu na Mfalme Maridadi, akikaribia kuliwa na vile vichwa vya joka.
Upande wa pili: Zuwena alikuwa anamsogelea baba yangu, kisu chake mkononi akitaka kumkata shingo.
"Shafih! Nisaidie!" Baba alilia.
​Niliushika kisu cha Malkia. Mkono wangu ulikuwa unatetemeka. Kila chembe ya ubinadamu ndani yangu ilikuwa inakataa maumivu yaliyokuwa yanakuja. Lakini nilipoona macho ya baba yanavyofumba, niliamua.
​Nilikipandisha kisu kile juu na kukichomeka katikati ya kile kovu langu linalowaka.
​"AAAAAAHHHHHHH!"
​Sauti yangu haikuwa yangu tena. Ilikuwa ni mlio wa dhoruba ya bahari kuu. Kutoka kwenye mkono wangu, nuru ya ajabu ya dhahabu ililipuka—si kama mwanga, bali kama wimbi la maji ya moto. Nuru ile ilimzunguka Nahodha, ikampa nguvu mpya, na ikamrusha Zuwena mbali na baba yangu.
​Mfalme Maridadi alitoa kioja cha maumivu wakati nuru ile ilipomgusa. Magamba yake yalianza kubadilika na kuwa mchanga. "Shafih! Unafanya nini? Utaangamiza mji wote!"
​"Mji uliojengwa kwa damu haustahili kusimama!" nilijibu, huku nikiinuka hewani. Mwili wangu ulikuwa unabadilika. Miguu yangu ilikuwa inapotea na kugeuka kuwa mkia mkubwa wa samaki wenye rangi ya dhahabu na fedha. Ngozi yangu yote ilikuwa imefunikwa na magamba yanayong'aa, na kifuani pangu, moyo ulikuwa unadunda kwa mwanga unaoonekana kwa nje.
​Mji wa Mafuvu ya Dhahabu ulianza kupasuka. Maji ya bahari ya kweli—maji ya baridi na ya chumvi—yalianza kuingia kwa kasi ndani ya lile pango.
​"Shafih, chukua baba yako! Kimbia!" Nahodha alipiga kelele huku akimkaba Mfalme Maridadi kwa mkuki wake, akijitoa mhanga ili sisi tuweze kutoroka.
​Niliogelea kwa kasi ya ajabu, kasi ambayo hakuna binadamu anaweza kuwa nayo. Nilimnyaka baba yangu aliyekuwa amezimia, nikamweka mgongoni. Nilitaka kumchukua na Malkia Bi. Subira, lakini alinitikisia kichwa kwa huzuni. "Hapa ndipo mwisho wangu, mwanangu Shafih. Linda bahari. Linda watu wako."
​Nilipokuwa naogelea kuelekea juu kwenye ule ufa, nilihisi kitu kikishika mkia wangu. Niliangalia chini. Alikuwa ni Zuwena. Uso wake sasa ulikuwa umerudi kuwa mrembo, macho yake yakiwa na majuto ya kweli.
​"Shafih... usiniache huku kwenye giza..." alinong'ona, huku mji ukiporomoka juu yake. "Nisamehe... nilikupenda kweli, lakini mimi ni mtumwa wa damu yangu."
​Nilipata mtikisiko wa moyo. Je, nimuache Zuwena azikwe na mji wa baba yake, au nimuokoe mke wangu ambaye amesababisha vifo na maumivu yote haya?
​Huku maji yakiwa yanazidi kuvurugika na miamba mikubwa ikianguka, niliuona uso wa Nahodha ukipotea kwenye giza la vilindi huku akipigana na joka la vichwa vitatu.
​Nilifika juu ya ufukwe wa Kichangani nikiwa nimebeba mwili wa baba yangu. Lakini nilipojiangalia kwenye maji ya ufukweni, nilipiga kelele. Sikuwa tena Shafih yule kijana mvuvi. Nusu yangu ya chini ilikuwa samaki, na nusu ya juu ilikuwa na magamba.
​Kijiji kilikuwa kimya. Ukungu wa kijani ulikuwa umepotea. Lakini mchanga wa bahari ulikuwa mwekundu kama damu.
​Shafih ameweza kumuokoa baba yake, lakini kwa gharama gani? Amepoteza ubinadamu wake, na Nahodha amebaki vilindini. Je, Zuwena alifanikiwa kutoka? Na nini kitatokea wakati wanakijiji watakapomwona Shafih katika umbo lake jipya la 'Mlinzi wa Bahari'?

Indira Devi Dhanrajgirji passed away yesterday at 96. I had posted this some years ago and Rajit Pillai very thoughtfully sent it to me. 
“PRINCELY LIFE IN HYDERABAD.
This was sent  to me by Krishnan Venugopal  who has a deep and abiding interest in old Hyderabad, and for that matter in anything old. Indira Devi Dhanrajgirji was known to my parents and was a prominent socialite in the post independence  Hyderabad state. She was extraordinarily beautiful and was always dressed in chiffon saris as was the norm with the ex-nobility. Whenever I drift into the Secunderabad Sailing Club on a Sunday morning my minds eye still takes me to looking at her on the lawns, elegant and ethereal.

This excerpt from her memoir is very revealing. Apart from the court etiquette and the details of the lifestyle of the times, it also tells us how isolated the small elite was from the world outside. Hyderabad had broad and we'll maintained tree lined roads  that led out of the city of great palaces and havelis. These grand roads ended a few miles outside and became potholed one lane tracks to the rest of Indias biggest princely state. The rest of the arid state existed in dire circumstances and with little trickle down from the government of the richest man on earth.

Indira Devi Dhanrajgiri: Audience with the Nizam.
(Reproduced from ‘Memories of the Deccan' by Indira Devi Dhanrajgiriji, with kind permission of the author.) 

I was thirteen then, studying at the Mahboobia Girls' School in Hyderabad. One day the governesses were ordered to to bring my brothers and me to the billiard room at 11 am to meet Papa. It was a Sunday and the day had begun like any other day. I had gone riding in the morning with Ibrahim Khan accompanying me on another horse. 

I wondered why we were summoned: usually, we were called only when one of us had to be reprimanded for some rudeness or carelessness we had shown. From the upstairs balcony I saw Uncle Khusro (Nawab Khusro Jung) having breakfast with Papa at the other end of the garden where the yellow flowering trees shielded the sun from scattering itself on the moist lawn. November had tiptoed into the garden; there was a healing coolness in the air known in Hyderabad as gulabi-jade (pink winter) or rosy winter. 

At 11 am my brothers Mahendragir and Dhairyavangir and I went down to the billiard room. Shankara Bai, the famous classical singer of Hyderabad, was sitting there, her sazindas waiting on the veranda outside. The chilbans which covered the doors of the room was an added protection from the glare outside. The chilban was soon lifted by the man in the peshi and Papa and Nawab Ahmed Baig entered. Papa greeted Shankara Bai and took a seat at the card table. 

We siblings did our namaskars and kissed Papa on both cheeks. Taking a paan from his gold paandan, Papa announced that the next day my brothers and I were to accompany him to King Koti to pay our respects to Ala Hazrath, the Nizam VII. 

There was silence. I could not understand why this was necessary. I had seen HEH the Nizam, Mir Osman Ali Khan Bahadur, often enough. He would go in his limousine to his mother's grave near Daru-shifa every evening. I used to watch with amazement as the police whistled all traffic to stop and everybody waited with baited breath for the royal car to pass. It was a thrilling spectacle. The entire road from King Koti to Daru-shifa would be stunned into a still silence. 

Now that we were going to be face to face with this exalted person, what was he going to be like? Handsome, tall and bewitching? Would he be like Maharaja Keshen Pershad with whom I played carom or like Uncle Salar Jung (Nawan Salar Jung Bahadur) who had given me my first Shetland pony on my first birthday? Perhaps he would be like Uncle Khudrat Nawaz Jung, brother-in-law of the Nizam. 

Khudrat Nawaz Jung Bahadur's sister was Dulhan Pasha, HEH Nizam's wife. I had also seen her shopping on Abid Road. Her car would come to a halt in front of a shop and if by accident anyone was seen loitering on the road or near her car, after the whistles had cleared the road, then she would order her secretary to get the person to take seven rounds of the car and then ask him to go. Only then would she come out of the limousine. She was a slim, tall and fair person and seemed to be always followed by a retinue. When she entered a shop the purdah was lowered while we huddled in a corner with our governesses. She was rumoured to be a kleptomaniac. However, the various articles she picked up were duly returned to the shops by the sarkar's peshi. 

Dulhan Pasha had two sons and a daughter: Prince Waleshan Azam Jah Bahadur, the eldest who married the regal Princess Dur-e-Shehwar of Turkey, the second son Prince Waleshan Moazzam Jah Bahadur, who married Princess Niloufer also from Turkey, and Shehzadi Pasha, the daughter, who did not marry but continued to live with her father. 

We were now in the music room with Divatia who we called Uncle Prince (he was Papa's personal secretary, and came from a distinguished family rom Gujarat). Among the beautiful portraits here is one of Papa done by an artist from the Royal Academy, London. She did one of me as a child and gifted it to my father which I still possess, but the one of me sitting on a Louis the XIV gold-leafed chair is lost. 

Hanging here, there is also a beautiful portrait of Mahboob Ali Pasha, the sixth Nizam. When I was young I was surrounded by stories about the great ruler. My father told me how when the Musi was in flood and the city was submerged in its dangerous water, Mahboob Ali Pasha was advised by Hindu purohits to perform yagna and pooja to the river in flood. The Muslim gentry opposed this suggestion, they said how can you wear a janev and sit for pooja as a kafir? To which Mahboob Ali Pasha replied, "Hindus and Muslims are my two eyes, besides, a ruler has no religion." He followed advice of the purohits and as he offered aarthi to the river it began to slowly recede and the city was saved. 

There is also a lovely oil painting of Mir Osman Ali Khan Bahadur, the seventh Nizam, as a young man. He's wearing a yellow dastar with a turra, adrak-coloured coat and sherwani. But his eyes had something special, I thought they glowed with intelligence. 

I turned to look at the portrait once more. So this was the person we were to face tomorrow. The very thought made me nervous. I was not accustomed to mingling with the grown-ups, but then His Exalted Highness the Nizam was another matter altogether. Papa's secretary was giving us our first lesson in court manners. "You all shall enter behind Raja Saheb, and stand at a distance from Ala Hazrath … then you will do the farshi adab. Begin from your waist and slowly bring your hand to the face, like this," he demonstrated. 

We knew what he meant because we had seen some people do this, to father and even us. "Not to speak unless spoken to" was the last command. Promptly bored with all this, my brothers ran into the garden to play with their friends and my mother called me to her bedroom to choose the sari I would wear on the special day. 

We wore French chiffon in those days straight from Paris, but because of World War II, they were not easily available. I had never worn a sari before. Mama chose a pale yellow chiffon embroidered with yellow and white shells in beautiful clusters which had been specially made for her by Madame Carosh of Bombay. They found a pair of two-inch-high gold-heeled shoes and sequence bag to match the ensemble, then the jewellery was decided upon. 

We even had a dress rehearsal: the sari was draped around my body, my mother's blouse was cut and stitched to fit me. Then the pallav was lightly draped over my head. It was a little uncomfortable taking small steps. I walked hesitatingly, afraid I might trip and cut a sorry figure. Our house itself had so many steps and how many would be in the palace I wondered. 

At precisely eleven o'clock the next day the Rolls Royce was ready. Abdul Lateef the chauffeur looked smart in his uniform as he stood to attention. My father wore a motia-pink pagdi, pale gray sherwani, white churidars, black shoes (not silam shahis), diamond buttons and a cabochon emerald ring on his right hand. My brothers were dressed almost identically. I came down from the other wing accompanied by my mother's lady companion, wearing the yellow sari and what seemed all the family heirlooms: huge 10 carat diamond ear-rings, a diamond necklace of large solitaires held by a diamond chain made by Cartier and more diamonds on the hands. I was in borrowed finery, all of it belonged to my grandmother. 

We sat in the car with Papa and in the next car came his personal secretary Divatia. He was to carry the beautiful silver and gold paandan which had condiments like elaichi, lavang, supari and dalchini all in gold. On the lids of each section and on top of the paandan was the royal emblem, the dastar, also in gold. When the car approached the gate of King Kothi we were reminded that we were to offer nazar to Ala Hazrath after Papa, which consisted of one gold ashrafi and four Hali Rupees. Papa was to give 11 ashrafis. 

We stepped into the courtyard of King Kothi. Except for a few trees here and there all was gravel … it didn't disturb me, my eyes were looking for the Nizam who I had only seen seated in his royal limousine with the Asaf Jahi flag fluttering in the air. All the number plates of the cars were painted yellow. We proceeded further to the right which was a raised platform, with a slanting roof, perhaps a temporary shed. There was a solitary person wearing a red Rumi topi. He was thin, his face was proud, his voice was authentic and clear. 

My father bent down and did his adab, we did the same from wherever we were standing which was just a few feet away from him. My father first, and then we offered nazrana. He put his hands on the coins and, when we insisted, picked up the gold ones and put them into a bag and the silver ones into another. 

He addressed my father. "Dhanraj, these are your children?" 
"Ji Sarkar. My eldest daughter and these two are my sons. I have a young daughter who is very small." 

The Nizam looked towards me. I was looking away, those were the instructions though now and again I managed to sneak a look at him from the corner of my eye when he was talking to others. 

"Do you go to school?" 
"Ji Your Exalted Highness." I timidly replied. 
"At Bombay or here?" he queried. 
"We were in Bombay but now I have joined Mahboobia." 
"Do you like it here? Do you find any difference in the education here?" 

I lifted my head lightly and answered him coolly, "I love Hyderabad but the education in Mahboobia is a little strange to me still. Perhaps it is because I have joined recently." 
"What class are you in at present?" 
"I am in the junior Cambridge" (Ji mai junior Cambridge mein hoon.) 
"Good, good … education is a must for girls," and turning to my father, "When did you all come from Bombay?" 
"A few months back the family moved back to Hyderabad." 

My father signaled to Divatia to bring the gift forward for HEH to see. This paandan had been ordered specially for him several years ago and had been kept safely in the silver room. 

HEH looked at it, touched it with his long fingers, he touched the solid gold supari, elaichis, lavangs and then touched the dastar, and a smile broke on his lips. 
"Where did you have this made?" 
"At Bangalore, and it was intended for your good self." 
"Hm hm I like it, it will be kept in the Jubilee Museum." His ADC came forward and whisked it away promptly saying, "Ji Malik, ji Sarkar." 

The Nizam's eyes were drawn again and again to the cabochon emerald ring on Papa's finger. It had a green fire in it, and the Nizam was famous for his emerald collection! I might mention here that in old Hyderabad under the Nizam there was no income-tax. Whenever the state needed funds to build railways, gold mines, airways or coal mines, the money was raised through certain families and repaid to them as agreed upon. We have servants who tell us that money came in cartloads and had to be weighed and stacked away in rooms. 

My young mind kept considering the august personality: his fluent manner of speaking, the authority in his voice showed that his education was not lacking. He was proficient in Urdu, Persian, Arabic and English and wrote poetry of a high order. His ustads were the famous Dagh Dehlvi and Jalaal Manikpuri, two great names. HEH ran a newspaper from the palace itself. Perhaps if he had not been the Nizam he would have been a literary stalwart. 

He clapped – and a cup of tea was brought for him in a simple china cup by his daughter Princess Shehzadi Pasha. He was known to drink umpteen cups of tea each day. He was smoking Charminar cigarettes, and he was a chain smoker. There seemed to be no chairs around. Yes, there was one solitary chair on the platform (chabutra) perhaps meant for him, but he kept standing. 

To my surprise, the Nizam in real life did not resemble the man in the portrait which has adorned our music room even to this day. The features were the same, the regalia, the dastar were missing, but his simplicity had put me at ease. I liked the person. It proved that the man was larger than what he possessed in terms of material wealth. 

We paid our obeisance and walked with our backs facing the entrance, as you know, you cannot show your back to the Nizam. The next day, a messenger brought a letter to Gyan Bagh from King Kothi. He had written a letter to my father thanking him for the present which he said would be placed in the Jubilee Museum and described me as "your handsome daughter." It was the first ever compliment paid to me! 

Whenever a dignitary visited Hyderabad there would be an official at-home held by the government. Important people of the state were presented to the dignitary at the entrance of the Jubilee Hall: Nawab and Begum Zahir Yar Jung Bahadur, Nawab and Begum Himayernawaz Jung Bahadur, Raja and Rani Pratapgiri Bahadur (my uncle), Raja Dhanrajgiri and I, as my father's official hostess as my mother was unwell. And on each occasion, the HEH would come and speak to me as I paid my obeisance. He took special pleasure in introducing me to the distinguished guests as the youngest in the gathering. He would proudly say: "I have known her since she was that high." 

By the time Lord Mountbatten came to Hyderabad I was a grown woman and had come a long way from the day I had first been inside the King Kothi for an audience with HEH Mir Osman Ali Khan, the seventh Nizam.”

Ufugaji wa kuku chotara au kuku wa kienyeji kwa njia huria ni miongoni mwa miradi rahisi, ya gharama nafuu na yenye faida kubwa endapo itasimamiwa vizuri.

🐔 Kuku chotara na kuku wa kienyeji ni akina nani?
Kuku wa kienyeji ni wale waliokomaa katika mazingira ya asili, wana uwezo mkubwa wa kustahimili magonjwa na mabadiliko ya hali ya hewa.
Kuku chotara ni mchanganyiko wa kuku wa kienyeji na wa kisasa (broiler au layer), hivyo huwa na sifa nzuri zote mbili: hukua haraka, hutaga mayai mengi kuliko wa kienyeji na bado wanastahimili mazingira.

🌿 Njia huria ni nini?
Ufugaji wa kuku kwa njia huria ni pale kuku wanapewa uhuru wa kutembea nje ya banda, kutafuta chakula cha asili kama wadudu, majani, mchanga na mabaki ya chakula cha nyumbani. Njia hii inapunguza sana gharama za chakula na matunzo.

Idadi kadhaa ya wafanyakazi wameelekezwa kuondoka katika kambi ya kijeshi ya Marekani ya Al Udeid iliyopo nchini Qatar, hatua ambayo imetajwa kuchukuliwa “kutokana na hali ya sasa ya mvutano wa kikanda.”

Taarifa hiyo ilitolewa siku ya Jumatano na Ofisi ya Kimataifa ya Habari ya Qatar, ikieleza kuwa hatua hiyo ni ya tahadhari na inalenga kulinda usalama wa watu na miundombinu muhimu ya nchi hiyo.

Kwa mujibu wa taarifa hiyo, serikali ya Qatar imeeleza kuwa inaendelea kutekeleza hatua zote muhimu ili kuhakikisha usalama na ulinzi wa raia wake pamoja na wakazi wote waliopo nchini humo.

Usalama huo umetajwa kuwa ni kipaumbele cha juu, hasa katika kipindi ambacho eneo la Mashariki ya Kati linakabiliwa na mvutano unaoendelea kuongezeka.

Taarifa hiyo pia ilisisitiza kuwa hatua hizo zinajumuisha ulinzi wa miundombinu muhimu ya kitaifa pamoja na vituo vya kijeshi vilivyopo nchini humo.

Kambi ya Al Udeid inajulikana kuwa ni kituo kikubwa zaidi cha kijeshi cha Marekani katika eneo la Mashariki ya Kati, na imekuwa na mchango mkubwa katika operesheni za kijeshi na kiusalama za Marekani na washirika wake katika kanda hiyo.

Hivyo basi, mabadiliko yoyote yanayohusu idadi ya wanajeshi au wafanyakazi katika kambi hiyo huvutia hisia na ufuatiliaji wa karibu kutoka kwa wachambuzi wa masuala ya usalama na diplomasia.

Maelezo haya yanaweka marekebisho ya hivi karibuni katika muktadha wa tahadhari, yakifuata ripoti za kidiplomasia zilizoeleza kuwa baadhi ya wafanyakazi waliokuwa katika kambi hiyo walishauriwa kuondoka kwa muda.

Ingawa hakukuwa na maelezo ya kina kuhusu asili ya tishio lolote la moja kwa moja, hatua hiyo imechukuliwa kama sehemu ya maandalizi ya kukabiliana na hatari zozote zinazoweza kujitokeza kutokana na hali ya kisiasa na kiusalama katika eneo hilo.

Serikali ya Qatar imejaribu kuwahakikishia raia na wakazi wake kuwa hali ya usalama nchini humo iko chini ya udhibiti, na kwamba hakuna sababu ya hofu.

 Aidha, imeeleza kuwa inaendelea kushirikiana kwa karibu na washirika wake wa kimataifa ili kuhakikisha utulivu na amani vinaendelea kudumishwa.

Hatua hii imekuja katika kipindi ambacho mvutano wa kisiasa na kijeshi unaendelea kushuhudiwa katika sehemu mbalimbali za Mashariki ya Kati, hali inayosababisha nchi nyingi kuchukua tahadhari za ziada.

Wachambuzi wanaona kuwa uamuzi wa kupunguza au kuhamisha baadhi ya wafanyakazi ni mkakati wa kawaida wa kiusalama unaolenga kuzuia hasara na kuhakikisha maandalizi ya haraka endapo hali itabadilika ghafla.

Wakati huo huo, macho ya dunia yanaendelea kuelekezwa Qatar na kambi ya Al Udeid, huku wengi wakisubiri kuona iwapo hali ya mvutano itapungua au itaendelea kuongezeka katika siku zijazo.

Vilevile, Waziri Mkuu amekemea tabia ya baadhi ya wenye nyumba kumpangisha raia mmoja wa kigeni na kumruhusu mpangaji huyo apangishe watu wengine ndani ya nyumba hiyo jambo ambalo ni hatari kwa usalama na pia halina tija kibiashara.
 
Mheshimiwa Dkt. Mwigulu ametoa agizo hilo leo Jumatano, Januari 14, 2026 alipofungua Kikao cha Mawaziri, Naibu Mawaziri, Makatibu Wakuu na Manaibu Makatibu Wakuu wa Wizara za Kisekta kujadili fursa za ajira ndani na nje ya nchi.
 
Agizo hilo linalenga kuongeza fursa za ajira kwa Watanzania kufuatia kuwepo kwa wimbi kubwa la wageni kufanya kazi au biashara ambazo zinaweza kufanywa na Watanzania na kuliwezesha Taifa kukabiliana na changamoto ya upungufu wa ajira.
 
“…Kazi zinazoweza kufanywa na Watanzania ziachwe wafanye, si kuruhusu wageni wafanye. Tusioneane aibu kama tumefungua milango au kulegeza wataalamu wafuatilie. Wageni wafanye kazi za kitaalamu ambazo nchi ina uhaba wa wataalamu.”
 
Amesema kuwa ni lazima wataalamu wa ndani wasimamie sheria ipasavyo na kama kuna maeneo yanayokwamisha wayabainishe na yafanyiwe marekebisho. “Hatuwezi kuleta watu wanaokuja kufanya kazi ambazo Watazania wanaziweza.”

Waziri Mkuu amewaagiza wahusika wafuatilie suala hilo la makazi ili wakae katika utaratibu ulio rasmi. “Eneo hili liangaliwe wageni wanalundikana na kufanya kazi ambazo Watanzania wangeweza kufanya, hatuwezi kuruhusu hili tunataka wawekezaji.”
 
Hivyo, Waziri Mkuu ameziagiza wizara zinazohusika zifuatilie suala hilo, pamoja na kuwasisitiza wasimamie utekelezwaji wa sheria kwa sababu kila nchi ina sheria zake na Tanzania inatekeleza majukumu yake kwa kufuata sheria.

How Isaiah Defines the "Line-upon-Line" Principle of Learning

As Isaiah is the first prophet to address the "line-upon-line" principle of learning, his words are key to understanding what it is. In an end-time prophecy directed at the "drunkards of Ephraim," their straying prophets and erring seers (Isaiah 28:1, 7), he decries their failure to advance beyond the infant stage of learning and their resultant incapacity to receive divine revelation:

"Whom shall he give instruction? Whom shall he enlighten with revelation? Weanlings weaned from milk, those just taken from the breast? For it is but line upon line, line upon line, precept upon precept, precept upon precept; a trifle here, a trifle there" (Isaiah 28:9–10). Paul echoes that idea when bidding the saints to move on from the milk of the gospel to the meat (Hebrews 5:12).

The Hebrew of "line upon line, line upon line, precept upon precept, precept upon precept" (tzav latzav tzav latzav qav laqav qav laqav) uses repetition, assonance, and alliteration to parody the rote method of learning—as in a kindergarten, where children are instructed to repeat after the teacher. Such a primitive mode of learning is uncommendable for a covenant people of God.

When the gospel's basic principles are regarded as its fulness, believers are in no way equipped to deal with imminent end-time challenges. Isaiah laments that "all tables [luach, also 'tablets'] are filled with vomit; no spot is without excrement" (Isaiah 28:8). Instead of being directly instructed by God, the people are fed half-digested food regurgitated for them to swallow.

Revelation begets God's rest: "This is rest; let the weary rest! This is a respite! But they would not listen. So to them the word of Jehovah remained: Line upon line, line upon line, precept upon precept, precept upon precept; a trifle here, a trifle there, that, persisting, they might lapse into stumbling and break themselves, become ensnared and be taken captive" (Isaiah 28:12–13).

Alma expresses a similar idea. He who pays heed and diligence to God will "know the mysteries of God until he know them in full," whereas "they that will harden their hearts, to them is given the lesser portion of the word until they know nothing concerning his mysteries; and then they are taken captive by the devil, and led by his will down to destruction" (Alma 12:9–11).

Isaiah warns of the same: "Jehovah will rise up as he did on Mount Perazim, and be stirred to anger, as in the Valley of Gibeon—to perform his act, his unwonted act, and do his work, his bizarre work. Now therefore scoff not, lest your bonds grow severe, for I have heard utter destruction decreed by my Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, upon the whole earth" (Isaiah 28:21–22).

This passage and entire chapter show up the retributive aspect of God's end-time "work": (1) that the destruction of the earth's wicked inhabitants—including, as in this case, the scoffers of Ephraim—occurs concurrently with the deliverance of those who find rest in God; and (2) that a general falling away of God's people is what triggers the world's end-time destruction.

The same pattern of God's people's atrophy led to former worldwide destructions, as when Assyria and later Babylon conquered the then-known world. In Isaiah's end-time scenario, it is Ephraim and its leaders' "Covenant with Death" —"taking refuge in deception and hiding behind falsehoods" when a scourge threatens—that causes it to overtake them (Isaiah 28:18).

Hence, the chief purpose of rote learning: "I will give unto the children of men line upon line, precept upon precept, here a little and there a little; and blessed are those who hearken unto my precepts, and lend an ear unto my counsel, for they shall learn wisdom; for unto him that receiveth I will give more"—more of his life-saving "word" and "truth" (2 Nephi 28:28–30). UTANGULIZI

Katika dunia iliyojaa mabadiliko, misukosuko, na hali zisizotabirika, kuna jambo moja lisilobadilika kamwe—MUNGU.            

Neno la Mungu linatupa ukweli wa milele unaotupa amani, tumaini, na uthabiti wa imani. Somo hili linatufundisha kweli 10 zisizotikiswa kuhusu Mungu wetu.

1. Upendo wa Mungu kwako hauwezi kuisha kamwe

(Warumi 8:38–39)
Kwa maana nimekwisha kujua hakika ya kwamba, wala mauti, wala uzima, wala malaika, wala wenye mamlaka, wala yaliyopo, wala yatakayokuwapo, wala wenye uwezo,
 wala yaliyo juu, wala yaliyo chini, wala kiumbe kinginecho chote hakitaweza kututenga na upendo wa Mungu ulio katika Kristo Yesu Bwana wetu. 

Hakuna jambo lolote—dhiki, mateso, mauti, maisha, au nguvu za giza—linaloweza kututenga na upendo wa Mungu ulio katika Kristo Yesu.

👉 Upendo wa Mungu haupimwi kwa hali unayopitia, bali kwa msalaba wa Yesu Kristo.

Fundisho: Usijione huna thamani; Mungu anakupenda bila masharti.

2. Mungu hachoki wala kudhoofika kamwe
(Isaya 40:28)
Je! Wewe hukujua? Hukusikia? Yeye Mungu wa milele, BWANA, Muumba miisho ya dunia, hazimii, wala hachoki; akili zake hazichunguziki. 

Mungu si kama mwanadamu anayechoka au kukata tamaa. Yeye ana nguvu zisizo na mwisho.

👉 Unapochoka, Mungu bado ana nguvu za kukubeba.

Fundisho: Tegemea nguvu za Mungu, si zako mwenyewe.

3. Rehema za Mungu haziishi kamwe

(Maombolezo 3:22–23)
Ni huruma za BWANA kwamba hatuangamii, 
Kwa kuwa rehema zake hazikomi. 
Ni mpya kila siku asubuhi; 
Uaminifu wako ni mkuu. 

Rehema za Bwana ni mpya kila asubuhi. Hata ukianguka leo, bado kuna rehema kesho.

👉 Mungu hajachoka kukusamehe unapokuja kwake kwa toba ya kweli.

Fundisho: Usikate tamaa kwa sababu ya makosa yako; rehema zipo.

4. Mungu hatakuacha wala hatakutenga kamwe

(Waebrania 13:5)
Msiwe na tabia ya kupenda fedha; mwe radhi na vitu mlivyo navyo; kwa kuwa yeye mwenyewe amesema, Sitakupungukia kabisa, wala sitakuacha kabisa. 

Watu wanaweza kukuacha, marafiki wakakugeuka, lakini Mungu hasemi uongo.
👉 Uwe peke yako kimwili, lakini si peke yako kiroho.

Fundisho: Uwepo wa Mungu ni wa kudumu katika maisha ya waaminio.

5. Kweli ya Mungu haibadiliki kamwe

(Waebrania 13:8)
Yesu Kristo ni yeye yule, jana na leo na hata milele. 

Yesu Kristo ni yeye yule jana, leo, na hata milele.

👉 Kile Mungu alichofanya zamani, anaweza kukifanya leo.

Fundisho: Neno la Mungu ni msingi thabiti wa maisha yako.

6. Mungu hashindwi kamwe na giza

(Mathayo 16:18)
Nami nakuambia, Wewe ndiwe Petro, na juu ya mwamba huu nitalijenga kanisa langu; wala milango ya kuzimu haitalishinda. 

Nguvu za kuzimu haziwezi kulishinda Kanisa la Kristo.

👉 Giza haliwezi kuuzima mwanga wa Mungu.

Fundisho: Usihofu nguvu za giza; Mungu yuko juu ya yote.

7. Ahadi za Mungu hazivunjiki kamwe
(Tito 1:2)
katika tumaini la uzima wa milele, ambao Mungu asiyeweza kusema uongo aliuahidi tangu milele; 

Mungu hawezi kusema uongo. Kila alichoahidi, atakitimiza kwa wakati wake.

👉 Kuna kuchelewa, lakini hakuna kusahau kwa Mungu.

Fundisho: Subiri kwa imani; ahadi bado ipo njiani.

8. Mipango ya Mungu haiwezi kuzuiwa

(Ayubu 42:2)
Najua ya kuwa waweza kufanya mambo yote, 
Na ya kuwa makusudi yako hayawezi kuzuilika. 
Hakuna mtu, pepo, au mazingira yanayoweza kusimamisha kusudi la Mungu juu ya maisha yako.

👉 Mungu akikusudia mema, hakuna wa kuyazuia.

Fundisho: Acha kuogopa vikwazo; Mungu ana neno la mwisho

9. Mungu si chanzo cha machafuko

(1 Wakorintho 14:33)
Kwa maana Mungu si Mungu wa machafuko, bali wa amani; vile vile kama ilivyo katika makanisa yote ya watakatifu. 

Pale palipo na Mungu, kuna amani, mpangilio, na mwelekeo.

👉 Machafuko hayatoki kwa Mungu, bali hutoka kwa adui au kukosa mwongozo wa Roho Mtakatifu.

Fundisho: Tafuta amani ya Mungu katika maamuzi yako.

10. Neema ya Mungu haikauki kamwe

(Waefeso 3:16)
awajalieni, kwa kadiri ya utajiri wa utukufu wake, kufanywa imara kwa nguvu, kwa kazi ya Roho wake katika utu wa ndani. 

Neema ya Mungu inatosha kila siku, katika kila hali.

👉 Pale dhambi ilipozidi, neema ilizidi zaidi.

Fundisho: Neema ya Mungu ndiyo nguvu ya kuishi maisha matakatifu.

Somo: “NITAJIPATIA UTUKUFU KWA FARAO”

#KUTOKA 14:17 “Nami, tazama, nitaifanya mioyo ya Wamisri kuwa migumu, nao wataingia na kuwafuatia, NAMI NITAJIPATIA UTUKUFU KWA FARAO, na kwa jeshi lake lote,” 

Baada ya miaka mingi Yusufu akafariki, akatokea mfalme mwingine ambaye alikuwa hamjui Yusufu, wala historia ya kwanini watu wake wako Misri. Huyo mfalme akaamuru wana wa Israeli watiwe katika utumwa mzito na kuteswa. Akajaribu hata kuwafanyia hila ili wasiongezeke, KUTOKA 1:6-11,12-14. 

Utawala ulipobadilika maisha ya wana wa Israeli yakaanza kubadilika. Ndivyo hivyo hata katika maisha yetu ya kawaida mambo yanaweza kubadilika; afya inaweza kubadilika ukaanza kuugua, ndoa ikaharibika, kukosa kazi na shida ambazo hukuzizoea kabla zikainuka kinyume nawe.

Tatizo lilianzia kwa Farao, mtu mmoja akaanza kuwa tatizo kwa jamii kubwa. Adui anaweza kuingia katika maisha yako ghafla, na vitu vikaanza kubadilika. Adui hana sababu anaweza kukutesa bila sababu yoyote ile. 

Anaweza kuondoa amani kwenye ndoa yako, anaweza kukuletea magonjwa, anaweza kukuletea laana, mikosi na balaa na kila unalolifanya halifanikiwi. Anaweza akajaribu kukuletea hata roho ya mauti, roho ya kukataliwa au ukafukuzwa kazi kwa ghafla na maisha yakabadilika kabisa. 

Yamkini hata sasa inawezekana nazungumza na mtu wa jinsi hiyo, maisha unayoishi yamebadilika. Mwanzo hukuwa na maisha haya ya kuumwa-umwa, shida na mateso. Hukuwahi kuishi maisha haya ya kudharauliwa na kuachwa na ndugu na marafiki.

Farao akaamuru wana wa Israeli watumikishwe bila kulipwa, nao wamisri wakawatumikisha wana wa Israeli kwa ukali na kuyafanya maisha yao kuwa uchungu kwa kazi ngumu. Hivi ndivyo alivyo Shetani pamoja na kazi ngumu unayoifanya kwenye biashara haoni shida kukufanya usione faida yoyote, maana hakuna pesa. 

Unafanya kazi lakini haujui mshahara unafanyia nini? Unafanya kazi mbalimbali ngumu lakini pesa inakoenda haijulikani. Hii ni kazi ya Farao mfalme wa Misri, Ibilisi.

Wana wa Israeli wakawa wanatumikishwa na kuteswa kwa amri ya Farao mfalme wa Misri. Unaweza ukawa kwenye utumwa mzito wa magonjwa na shida, kumbe kuna amri imetolewa na adui kwamba mtu huyu adhibitiwe asipate kazi, asione tumaini, ateswe. 

Ndio maana leo ukimwamini Yesu wote waliotoa amri kwamba uteswe watapambana na mkono wa Bwana. Mungu alimbariki Ibrahimu na akaapa kwa nafsi yake kwamba atauzidisha uzao wake, MWANZO 22:15-18. 

Hivyo pamoja na amri ya Farao kuwazuilia wana wa Israeli wasiongezeke, pamoja na mateso na kazi ngumu za uchovu bado watu hawa walizidi kuongezeka, kuenea, kuzidishwa na kuzaana. 

Yaani kwa kadiri walivyoteswa ndivyo walivyoongezeka. Kwanini? Ahadi yake Mungu lazima itimie kama alivyosema, maana yeye si mtu aseme uongo, tena si mwanadamu ajute. Akihaidi amehaidi. Shetani na majeshi yake hawezi kuzuia kusudi la Mungu.

Hata kwako leo Bwana Yesu anaenda kuingilia kati, hata kama walizuia kwamba hautaongezeka kiuchumi, cheo, elimu, watoto ahadi yake Mungu lazima itimie kama alivyosema haijalishi mazingira yako yakoje. 

Nani mfalme huyu wa Misri Ibilisi anayejaribu kuzuia kusudi la Mungu juu yako, kwamba usiolewe, usizae, usipate kazi; kwa kutiwa mafuta ya Roho Mtakatifu kila nira katika maisha yako inaenda kuvunjwa sasa, na wewe unaenda kuwekwa huru. 

Leo kwa jina la Yesu biashara yako inaenda kuzidishwa, uzao wako unaenda kuzidishwa, afya yako inaenda kuzidishwa, elimu yako inaenda kuzidishwa, huduma yako inaenda kuzidishwa na kuongezeka katika jina la Yesu. 

Hakuna wa kumzuia Mungu kutenda, yeye ni mwenye nguvu na uweza wote. Hakuna wa kushindana na kusudi la Mungu juu yako, AYUBU 42:2.

“Honey,” nilinong’ona kwa sauti ya upole, moyo wangu ukiwa mzito. “Tafadhali endelea. Tuambie ukweli wote. Hakuna tena haja ya kuficha chochote.”

Alitikisa kichwa taratibu, macho yake yakiwa mazito kwa hofu na uchovu. “Sawa… nitasema,” alinena kwa sauti ya chini. Akavuta pumzi ndefu, akajaribu kuongea, lakini maneno yakamkwama kooni. Midomo yake ilitetemeka, jasho likamtoka ghafla 😰.

Nilihisi baridi ikinipitia. “Honey, unaendeleaje?” niliuliza kwa wasiwasi, lakini hakunijibu. Alijaribu tena kuzungumza, ila sauti haikutoka.
Ghafla, baba yake aliyekuwa amesimama mbele yetu alicheka kicheko cha kutisha 😈. “Nilikwambia… huu ni mwanzo tu. Yule anayefuatilia maiti kwa tamaa, mwisho wake huzikwa pamoja nayo.”

“Imefika mwisho!” alisema kwa sauti thabiti mtumishi wa dini kijana aliyekuwa amewaita wazazi wangu. Alisimama kwa ujasiri ✝️.
Baba mkwe alimkatiza kwa kejeli. “Wewe kaa chini! Usithubutu kuzungumza nikiwa bado nimesimama hapa.”
Hofu ilinijaa 😨.

Lakini mtumishi wa dini hakurudi nyuma. Alisogea mbele kwa utulivu wa ajabu. “Ninaweza kuonekana mdogo,” alisema kwa sauti yenye mamlaka, “lakini yule aliye ndani yangu ni Mkuu kuliko wote walioko duniani.”
Akageuka kumkabili mume wangu. “Kwa jina la Mungu Mkuu, ninakutangaza huru. Kila kifungo na kila laana imevunjika. Kuanzia leo, wewe ni huru.”

Mara upepo mkali ukavuma ndani ya chumba 🌬️, ukaleta harufu ya mvua. Radi ikagonga kwa mbali ⛈️. Jirani yetu alionekana dirishani, akichungulia kwa hofu.

Baba mkwe alianza kutetemeka, akashika kichwa chake kwa maumivu makali, kisha akaanguka kwenye kochi 😖.
Ndipo sauti ya mume wangu ikarudi, nzito na yenye huzuni. “Nitakiri,” alisema polepole. “Nakula gizani kwa sababu chakula nilichokiona kwenye mwanga hubadilika… huwa kinageuka minyoo 🐛. Na sikula peke yangu… kila mara kulikuwa na mtu mwingine. Kwa miaka kumi, sijawahi kuonja chakula cha kawaida.”

Chumba kizima kikanyamaza. Pumzi za mshangao zikagandia hewani 😱.
Mtumishi wa dini alituombea mimi, mume wangu na nyumba yetu. Alipomaliza, alitabasamu kwa upole. “Sasa yote yameisha. Ishini kwa amani 🤍.”

Baba mkwe alipelekwa nyumbani akiwa dhaifu sana. Njiani, tulimwona jirani akihamisha mizigo yake kwa haraka, akiondoka kimya kimya 🧳.

Kesho yake, tukapata taarifa kuwa baba mkwe alikuwa mgonjwa mahututi. Tulikimbilia kumwona.

“Baba,” mume wangu alisema akiwa kando ya kitanda, “acha hizi desturi. Bila hivyo, utapata amani.”

Kwa sauti dhaifu sana, alinong’ona: “Kamwe sitaacha… ni heri nife nikiwa nazo.”
Dakika chache baadaye… akafariki 🕊️.
Tulilia, tukahuzunika, lakini baada ya machozi kukauka, maisha yaliendelea.

Nilipika chakula. Kwa mara ya kwanza baada ya muda mrefu, tulikaa mezani tukala pamoja kwa furaha 🍲✨.
Siku moja jioni nikamchezea kimzaha: “Honey, nifungue taa?”

Alicheka, akanivuta karibu ❤️. “Usithubutu. Mimi sasa si mtoto wa giza tena… mimi ni mtoto wa mwanga.”

Miezi michache baadaye, furaha ilitugonga tena. Nilijifungua mapacha 👶👶. Tuliwapa majina David na Esther, ishara ya ushindi, imani na nuru baada ya dhoruba.

A gospel station hummed softly from the living room—CeCe Winans, her voice like velvet faith. Denise lifted her arm to stir a pot of gumbo and paused when her wrist felt strangely weak, like the spoon was heavier than it should’ve been.

She told herself she was tired.

She’d beaten worse.

She’d beaten cancer twice.

In the mirror, she saw a woman who’d survived too much to be scared of anything.

And yet her hands trembled.

Because she knew what it meant when your body begins to whisper.

It’s not asking.

It’s warning.

That’s the part nobody tells you after remission—that once you’ve fought death, you live with it listening.

“Who Was Leaving Fresh Milk and Bread at My Door Every Morning? When I Discovered the Secret of That Lonely Farmer, My Soul Trembled!”

Some stories begin as small mysteries—quiet gestures that no one understands at first, but which ultimately reveal deep and unsettling truths. This is the story of a widow who found milk and freshly made bread (or rolls) at her doorstep every day, and of a solitary farmer who was hiding a secret powerful enough to change everything.

It was September 2019, in a small village called Rampur in Uttar Pradesh, where everyone knew everyone else and keeping secrets was nearly impossible.

In that village lived Meera Sharma, a 34-year-old widow who had lost her husband, Aditya, in a road accident two years earlier. Aditya was a police constable who died while chasing a criminal. He left behind Meera and their three young children—Aryan, aged eight; Isha, five; and little Kabir, only two years old. The pension Meera received was very small, barely enough to pay the rent of their modest house on the edge of the village and cover basic living expenses.

Meera worked washing dishes and sweeping floors in other people’s homes, but the money was never enough. There were many days when the children went to school having eaten only dry bread with salt. Meera often skipped her own meals so her children could eat. She never asked anyone for help; her self-respect would not allow it. But everyone in the village knew that the martyred constable’s wife was living in hardship.

One Monday morning, when Meera woke up early to go to work and opened her door, she noticed a bag on her doorstep for the first time.

Inside was warm, freshly made homemade bread wrapped in a clean cloth, and a bottle of fresh milk. Meera looked around, hoping to catch a glimpse of someone, but the lane was empty. It was only 5:30 a.m., and the sun had not fully risen yet. “Who could it be?” she murmured as she picked up the bag. There was no note, no name—just milk and bread.

That day, the children ate breakfast with great delight. Aryan devoured the bread with butter, Isha drank the milk as if it were the best thing in the world, and little Kabir smiled as he ate.
“Mom, where did this come from?” Aryan asked.
“I don’t know, my son,” Meera replied, “but it’s a blessing from God.”

Meera thought it must be a one-time thing—perhaps an anonymous act of kindness from a good neighbor. But on Tuesday morning, when she opened the door, the same bag was there again. And then again on Wednesday, and again on Thursday. Every single morning, without fail, milk and bread appeared at her doorstep.

Meera grew increasingly confused. Who was doing this, and why? She asked the neighbors, but no one knew anything. She began waking up even earlier, determined to catch the person in the act. But even when she opened the door at five in the morning, the bag was already there, as if it had been placed in even deeper darkness.

“This is very strange,” her friend Radha said one evening. “Someone leaves food every day and doesn’t even reveal their name.”
“I know,” Meera replied, “but the children are eating better now. I can’t complain.”
“But Meera, this could also be dangerous…” Radha warned her.

UFAFANUZI WA KIBIBLIA KUHUSU SABATO NA JUMAPILI

Utangulizi
Miongoni mwa hoja zinazotumiwa sana na wanaoshikilia Sabato (Waasabato), ni madai kwamba Mfalme Konstantino wa Rumi ndiye aliyebadili siku ya ibada kutoka Sabato kwenda Jumapili.
Lakini swali la msingi ni hili:
Biblia inasemaje?
Kanisa la awali lilifundishwa na nani?
Na ushahidi wa Maandiko unaonyesha nini?
Makala hii inachunguza suala hili kwa Biblia, si kwa mapokeo ya kidini wala propaganda za kihistoria.

1. SABATO ILITOLEWA KWA ISRAELI KAMA KUMBUKUMBU YA KUTOLEWA MISRI
Biblia iko wazi: Sabato ilikuwa ishara ya Agano kati ya Mungu na Israeli, si mataifa yote.
“Waambie wana wa Israeli, mkisema, Hakika mtazishika Sabato zangu; maana ni ishara kati yangu na ninyi katika vizazi vyenu.”
(Kutoka 31:13)
Sabato haikupewa kama kumbukumbu ya uumbaji pekee, bali hasa:
“Ukumbuke ya kuwa ulikuwa mtumwa katika nchi ya Misri, naye BWANA Mungu wako akakutoa huko… kwa hiyo BWANA Mungu wako amekuagiza ushike siku ya Sabato.”
(Kumbukumbu la Torati 5:15)
➡ Sabato = kumbukumbu ya ukombozi wa Israeli kutoka Misri

2. YESU KRISTO ALILETA UKOMBOZI MPYA — SI WA MISRI, BALI WA DHAMBI
Agano Jipya linafunua ukombozi wa juu zaidi:
“Naye atawakomboa watu wake na dhambi zao.”
(Mathayo 1:21)
Ukombozi huu haukumbukwi kwa siku ya Sabato ya Agano la Kale, bali kwa ufufuo wa Kristo, ambao ulitokea:
“Hata siku ya kwanza ya juma…”
(Mathayo 28:1)
➡ Jumapili = siku ya ushindi, ushuhuda, na uzima mpya

3. YESU ALIFUFUKA SIKU YA KWANZA YA JUMA (JUMAPILI)
Biblia inasisitiza mara kwa mara:
Mathayo 28:1
Marko 16:2
Luka 24:1
Yohana 20:1
Zote zinasema:
“Siku ya kwanza ya juma”
Hakuna andiko hata moja linalosema:
“Yesu alifufuka siku ya Sabato.”
➡ Imani ya Wakristo inasimama juu ya ufufuo, si Sabato.
“Kama Kristo hakufufuka, basi kuhubiri kwetu ni bure.”
(1 Wakorintho 15:14)

4. KANISA LA AWALI LILIKUTANA NA KUVUNJA MKATE JUMAPILI
Hili lilitokea karne ya kwanza, kabla Konstantino hajazaliwa.
“Hata siku ya kwanza ya juma, tulipokutana kuvunja mkate…”
(Matendo ya Mitume 20:7)
Huu ulikuwa:
Mkutano wa Wakristo
Kuvunja mkate (Meza ya Bwana)
Mafundisho ya mitume
➡ Huu ni ushahidi wa moja kwa moja wa ibada ya Jumapili ilifanyika katika Kanisa la awali

Mtume Paulo anaandika:
“Siku ya kwanza ya juma kila mmoja wenu na aweke akiba…”
(1 Wakorintho 16:2)
Kwa nini si Sabato?
Kwa sababu: ➡ Jumapili ilikuwa siku ya kukutana kwa kanisa

6. JUMAPILI ILIJULIKANA KAMA “SIKU YA BWANA”
Mtume Yohana anaandika:
“Nalikuwa katika Roho siku ya Bwana.”
(Ufunuo 1:10)
Hakusema:
siku ya Sabato
siku ya Musa
➡ Siku ya Bwana = siku ya Kristo aliyefufuka

Hapana❌

Aliipa Jumapili mapumziko ya kiserikali

Paulo anaonya wazi:

Na tena:

Let me take you back to the classroom of history to explain why I, a woman of Nilotic roots, am so obsessed with Procedure, while some of my friends are obsessed with Material Results.

1. The Kingdom and the Council

The Luo, River-Lake Nilotes, trace our story to the civilizations of the Nile and Egypt. We had kings, Ruoth or Rwath, but they were never lawless. A king had to be brave, wise, and ethical. He was guided by a Council of Elders who could rebuke him privately and harshly if he strayed.

That is why you hear leaders like Raila Odinga insist, “Uchaguzi bora, sio bora uchaguzi” a quality election, not just any election. In our DNA, the process defines the product.

2. The Meritocracy of the Mountain

Among the Gikuyu, there were no central kings. Power was decentralized among councils and chiefs. Leadership often followed wealth. If you accumulated much, you became a Mutongoria or Muthamaki. But there was a rule: lose your wealth, and you lost your leadership.

This shaped a culture where acquisition is proof of ability. If the chapati is cooking, the Mountain is content. Riches are seen as the visible fruit of leadership.

3. The Conflict of Values

This is where the friction comes from:
 • In my tradition, wisdom, ethics, and the right way matter more than money. We want to know how you got it.
 • In the other tradition, results are the evidence of leadership. The means can be messy, as long as the ends are visible.

I come from a culture that believes a king without ethics is no king at all. That is why staged success does not mesmerize me. I am looking for the Ruoth of systems, a leadership brave enough to follow the law even when it is slow.

I do not hate success. I simply refuse to bow to a headless form of leadership that crowns riches and forgets the people.

Niliinamisha kichwa changu kutoa heshima kwa Malkia Ada.

"Nadhani Mimi na Malkia Shamsa tulikufukuza, kwanini umerudi hapa " Malkia Ada aliniuliza.

Nilipokosa jibu alimgeukia Mfalme.

"Pangani, naweza kujua kwanini bini huyu mwizi karudishwa hapa au kaletwa kuchinjwa "

"Hapana.....kama hauna haraka huko uendako unaweza kurudi ndani. Nitatoa tamko kuhusu huyu binti " Mfalme aliongea.

"Kwa kuwa najali kuhusu usalama wa Taifa hili nitarudi ndani...." Malkia Ada alimpa ishara Mtabiri Mkuu wakageuza miguu yao.

Kabla ya kutangazwa rasmi kuhusu vyeo vyangu nilibadilisha mavazi.

Mlinzi alikuja kunichukua akanipeleka kwenye ukumbi wa baraza la Mawaziri ambako Mfalme huendesha vikao vyake.

Nilitoa heshima kwa kuinamisha kichwa changu.

Ile Mfalme anataka kuongea Malkia Shamsa alifika. Ilimlazimu kusitisha kwanza mpaka Mkewe alipokaa.

"Kuanzia sasa na kuendelea huyu binti atakuwa ni Kijakazi wangu pamoja na Mpishi wangu " Mfalme aliongea, nilitarajia atayapima maneno kwa vitendo lakini alinipitisha moja kwa moja kuwa nitakuwa Mpishi wake.

"Nakataa " Malkia Shamsa alipinga.

"Kwanini "

"Huyu ni mwizi alipora nguo ya Kijana wangu pamoja n hereni za Malkia Ada.....nilimfukuza tafadhali sana naomba asirudishwe mahali hapa " Malkia Shamsa aliongea.

"Unawezaje kupinga amri ya Mfalme? mbona ni kama unavuka mipaka Malkia au una sumbuliwa na wivu " Malkia Ada aliingilia kati.

"Ni...ni...ni... nisamehe, nadhani akili yangu haipo sawa " Malkia Shamsa alijitetea.

Sijui na wengine waliona lakini nilimshuhudia Malkia Shamsa akikonyezana macho na Ada....Sikujua wanapanga nini.

Nilipitishwa rasmi kuwa Mpishi wa Mfalme pamoja na Kijakazi wake na hakuna mtu mwingine aliyejaribu kupinga tena.

Niliamua kuthibitisha maneno yangu kuwa naliweza jiko kwa kuandaa chakula cha mchana.

Huwa siliogopi jiko lakini siku ya leo nilijikuta ni kitetemeka Mb...wa Mimi, nilijizuia kuficha mtetemo wangu nisije umbuka.

Unajua huwa napika chakula kimzaha mzaha hivi. Yaani ukiniangalia vibaya unaweza kusema hakuna kitu nafanya.

Ndani ya dakika 20 chakula kilikuwa tayari.
Niliamriwa kukionja chakula nami nilifanya hivyo, lengo ni kupima kama kina sumu au la.

Vilikuwa ni vijiko viwili tu lakini nilijikuta ni kizidisha. Nilikula vijiko sita.

Mfalme aliachia kicheko, watu wote tulicheka pia.
Alionekana kufurahia chakula changu kuliko kawaida.

Mida ya usiku nikiwa najiandaa kulala, mlango wangu uligongwa....aliingia Mfalme. Japo suruali yake ni mapana kama ya dobi masumbuko lakini nililishuhudia dudu lake likiwa limenyooka kama rula.

Mie huyu nilitulia nione ni nini anataka kufanya...

ENDELEA.....

Nilijikuta nikikosa namna, Mfalme alinibana kona zote. Na Mimi na hisia bhana nilitoa ushirikiano. Tena kwa wakati huu niliibugia yote....

Mfalme ni mayowe tu ya utamu nami ndio nilizidisha manjonjo.

Niliikalia nikawa naitawala navyotaka niliipeleka kushoto na kulia, magharibi na kaskazini hadi akaanza kuongea lugha ambayo Mimi sielewi hata kidogo.

Mtumeeeeeee si nilisahau kufunga mlango. Tunu kijakazi wa Malkia Shamsa aliingia.
Basi hata aogope sasa hakufanya hivyo badala yake aliangaza macho kwa ukaribu. Baada ya kuiona sura ya Mfalme alianguka chini kuomba rehema.

Hatukuwa na hamu ya kuendelea na ya kuendelea na tendo.

Tunu alifumba macho yake Mfalme akajisitiri.

"Siwezi kukuambia kipi ufanye, kuishi au kufa ni juu yako " Mfalme slimtishia Tunu kiakili.

"Mimi huyu nahapia kwenye kaburi la marehemu Baba yangu siwezi kuzungumza chochote kwa Malkia Shamsa wala Ada. Na ikitokea nimetoa siri ndotoni basi ninyongwe Mimi " Tunu alitoa ahadi huku akilia.

"Sijui ni kitu gani kilikuleta unaweza kuongea " Mfalme aliongea.

"Malkia Shamsa anamuita Sadia" Tunu aliongea kwa kujing'ata ng'ata.

Nilivaa kwa kujisitiri ni kafuatana na Tunu.
Nilijikuta ni kikosa amani hasa nikifikiria Tunu anaweza kuropoka kitu ikala kwangu.

"Mbona macho yako hayatulii, usiniambie kuna kitu umefanya " Malkia Shamsa aliniuliza huku akimkabidhi Ivan kwa Kijakazi mwingine.

Sikujua lengo lake ni nini alianza kunisogelea taratibu. Mmmmh eti alinikumbatia akawa ananinusa nusa.

"Unanukia marashi ya Mfalme, usiniambie kuna kitu kimetokea kati yenu 🙄" Malkia Shamsa alifoka huku akijitoa kwangu.

Niongee nini Mimi sasa niliendelea kukaa kimya.

"Huyu huwa ana tabia ya kukaa kimya anapoulizwa vitu vya maana....hebu naomba uniambie ni kitu gani kinaendelea umemkuta huyu katika hali gani" Malkia Shamsa aliuliza.

"Alikuwa amelala " Tunu aliongea.

"Unanitania " Malkia Shamsa aliongea kisha akashika kisu alikiweka shingoni kwa Tunu.

"Nauliza kwa mara ya mwisho endapo hautatoa majibu yanayo eleweka na kutoboa hilo shingo na kisu" Alimtishia.

Tunu ni muoga balaa, alifumba macho yake kisha akazungumza kila kitu.

Mimi ni nani hata niendelee kusimama, nilidondoka chini kuomba rehema.

"Ondokeni wote " Malkia Shamsa alitufukuza.

Tuliendelea kusimama ilihali tuna tetemeka, sikujua ni kitu gani kinamtetemesha Tunu ilihali hajatenda ubaya wowote.

"Hamtaki kuondoka 🙄 basi nitaondoka Mimi" Malkia Shamsa aliongea kisha akaondoka yeye.

Tunu alinigeukia kwa hasira
"Hivi unajua ulichokifanya? tafuta kamba ujinyonge mapema tofauti na hapo utakuwa kwenye hatari kubwa nikimaanisha wewe pamoja na watu wa ukoo wako"

"Kujinyonga hapana siwezi kufa kwa sababu sijafanya ubaya wowote, Mfalme mwenyewe ndio alikuja chumbani kwangu. Ningewezaje kukataa na huku alinipatia amri nifanye naye mapenzi " Nilijitia kulia.

Tunu aliondoka akaniacha bila shaka alienda kumtafuta Malkia Shamsa. Sikuona sababu ya kuendelea kukaa malangoni kwa Malkia niliondoka.

Ile natoka tu nilidakwa na Vijakazi wa Malkia Ada. Walinibeba juu juu kana kwamba naenda kuchinjwa.
Nilijikuta ni kiogopa, baada ya kuingia malangoni kwa Malkia Ada nilimwagwa chini.

HE THREW A BUCKET OF FILTHY WATER ON A SCREAMING PUPPY, NOT REALIZING A VETERAN WAS RECORDING EVERY SECOND FROM THE DRIVEWAY.

I didn't move to this neighborhood to make friends. I moved here because the realtor promised me silence. After three tours overseas and a medical discharge that felt more like an eviction notice from my own life, silence was the only currency I cared about. I wanted a porch where I could drink my black coffee, a lawn that didn't hide IEDs, and neighbors who kept their business behind their fences.

But silence is heavy. It amplifies things. It makes the snap of a twig sound like a rifle bolt. And it makes the whimper of a terrified animal sound like a siren screaming in a church.

It started three days ago. The yelping. High-pitched, desperate, the sound of something small that doesn't understand why it's in pain. It came from the house to my right—a two-story colonial with peeling white paint and a lawn that was manicured with an aggressive, almost angry precision. The owner, a man named Gary, was the kind of guy who washed his truck twice a week but never looked you in the eye. He was soft in the middle but loud with his mouth, the type who yelled at the grocery bagger for squishing the bread.

I was sitting on my front steps, staring at the steam rising from my mug, when the back door next door slammed open. The sound cracked through the morning air like a gunshot.

I didn't flinch—I don't flinch anymore—but my head turned. The fence between us is waist-high chain link near the front, offering zero privacy. Through the gaps in the hedge, I saw him. Gary. He was red-faced, wearing a stained undershirt, carrying a yellow plastic bucket that sloshed with gray, murky water. It smelled like bleach and stagnation, a scent that drifted even over the fresh cut grass.

"Shut that thing up!" he screamed. It wasn't just frustration; there was a jagged edge of malice in his voice.

And then I saw the target. A puppy. Maybe ten weeks old, some kind of shepherd mix, huddled in the corner where the house met the garage. It was shaking so hard its ribs looked like they were vibrating. It wasn't barking. It was crying. It was backed into the brickwork, trying to make itself disappear.

Gary didn't hesitate. He heaved the bucket forward. The water hit the animal with a heavy, slapping sound. The puppy didn't run—it just collapsed flat against the concrete, letting out a gargled choke as the dirty water flooded its nose and mouth.

"I said shut up!" Gary roared, kicking the empty bucket across the driveway. "You want to whine? Now you got a reason."

Something in my chest clicked. It was a mechanical sensation, like a safety switch flipping from 'safe' to 'fire'. My coffee mug hit the wood of my porch steps. I didn't realize I’d dropped it until I heard the ceramic shatter.

I stood up. My knees popped. My back hurt, the old injury flaring up, but the pain felt distant, like it was happening to someone else. I reached into my pocket and pulled out my phone. I didn't run over there screaming. Screaming is for people who are scared or people who want attention. I wasn't scared, and I didn't want attention. I wanted evidence.

I walked down my driveway, gravel crunching rhythmically under my boots. It was the only sound I made. I held the phone steady, the red recording dot pulsing on the screen. I captured the puppy shivering in the puddle of filth. I captured Gary wiping his hands on his pants, looking satisfied, like he’d just fixed a leaky pipe instead of assaulting a baby animal.

I crossed the property line. 

Gary looked up. He squinted against the sun, his bravado instantly checking itself when he saw me. We’d never spoken. He only knew me as the guy who stared at the wall for hours. He didn't know about the deployments. He didn't know about the things I’d done to keep men like him safe while they slept in their soft beds.

"Can I help you?" Gary asked. His voice was defensive, loud. He puffed his chest out, trying to reclaim the space.

I didn't answer. I kept walking. The distance between us closed—thirty feet, twenty, ten. I didn't stop until I was close enough to smell the stale coffee on his breath and the fear sweating out of his pores.

"I said, can I help you? Get off my property," he snapped, though he took a half-step back. He looked at the phone in my hand, then up at my face. I wasn't recording anymore. I slipped the phone into my pocket.

"You dropped something," I said. My voice surprised me. It wasn't loud. It was a low rumble, scraping the bottom of my throat. It sounded like the engine of a tank idling before the assault.

Gary blinked, confused. "What?"

I pointed to the puppy. The poor thing was trying to lick the dirty water off its fur, shivering violently. "Your humanity. You dropped it right there."

Gary’s face flushed a deeper shade of crimson. "Look, buddy, mind your own business. The mutt won't shut up. I'm training it."

"That's not training," I said, taking another step. He was backed up against the fender of his truck now. "That's torture."

"It's my dog!" he shouted, trying to summon anger to cover his cowardice. "I'll do what I want with it! Who do you think you are? Some kind of hero?"

I looked him up and down. I let the silence stretch. I let him look at the scars on my arms, the way I stood with my weight balanced, ready to move, ready to end this if he twitched the wrong way. I saw his eyes dart to my hands, then to my face. He saw it then. The look. The look that says I have walked through valleys you only see in nightmares.

"I'm the guy who's going to make you regret this," I said softly. "Pick it up."

"What?" 

"The towel," I said, nodding to a rag on his truck bed. "Dry the dog off."

"I'm not doing—"

I didn't yell. I didn't hit him. I just stepped into his personal space, invading the air he breathed. I leaned down, my face inches from his. "Dry. The. Dog. Off. Or we're going to have a very different conversation. One where I don't use words."

His knees actually shook. I saw the fabric of his cargo shorts tremble. The bluster evaporated. He grabbed the towel with shaking hands. He walked over to the puppy. The dog cowered, pressing itself into the brick, expecting another hit. It broke my heart more than the water did.

Gary looked at me, waiting for permission to stop. I didn't give it. I stood there, a statue of judgment, watching a grown man crumble under the weight of his own shame and the threat of consequences he couldn't even begin to calculate. 

"Gently," I commanded. 

He wiped the dog. He was terrified. Not of the dog, but of the man standing five feet away, watching him with eyes that had seen too much death to tolerate cruelty.

"Now," I said, pulling my phone back out. "We're going to sit right here and wait for the police. And if you move, Gary... if you so much as blink wrong... I’m going to consider it a threat."

He sat on the damp concrete. I stood over him. The puppy looked at me, confused, wet, and shivering. I winked at the little guy. 

Help was coming. But for now, I was the help.

Below is an honest and culturally grounded historical background of the Kimeitek clan, based on Kalenjin oral traditions, especially among the Kipsigis and Nandi. Because clan histories were preserved orally, some details vary slightly by region—but the core origin remains consistent.
Historical Background of the Kimeitek Clan
1. Origin and Meaning of the Name
The Kimeitek clan is a Kalenjin clan, predominantly found among the Kipsigis, with close links to the Nandi community.
The name Kimeitek is believed to derive from the Kalenjin word “meit”, meaning fire or burning, symbolizing strength, resilience, and endurance. Traditionally, fire represented protection, unity, and survival—key values associated with the clan.
2. Ancestral Roots
According to oral history, the Kimeitek trace their ancestry to early Nilotic Kalenjin ancestors who migrated southwards from the Upper Nile region (present-day South Sudan) between the 15th and 17th centuries.
During these migrations:
Kimeitek ancestors settled first around Mount Elgon and the Nandi Escarpment.
Later, some groups moved into present-day Kericho, Bomet, and Sotik areas as pasture and fertile land attracted them.
The clan emerged as a distinct lineage within the broader Kalenjin framework as families expanded and took clan identities based on lineage, occupation, or symbolic events.
3. Settlement Patterns
Historically, Kimeitek families were known to inhabit:
Kericho Highlands
Bomet and Chepalungu
Parts of Sotik and Nandi Hills
They preferred well-watered highlands, suitable for pastoralism and later mixed farming.
4. Social Role and Identity
Traditionally, members of the Kimeitek clan were:
Pastoralists (cattle, sheep, goats)
Protectors and warriors, especially during periods of inter-clan conflicts and cattle raids
Custodians of fire and homestead rituals, where fire symbolized continuity of life and lineage
Elders played a strong role in conflict resolution, marriage negotiations, and spiritual guidance.
5. Cultural Practices
Marriage: The Kimeitek strictly observed exogamy—marrying outside the clan to maintain kinship balance.
Initiation (Tumdo): Boys underwent circumcision rites that marked transition to warriorhood and adulthood.
Spiritual Beliefs: Like other Kalenjin, they worshipped Asis (God), associating fire and the sun with divine presence.
6. Colonial and Post-Colonial Era
During British colonial rule:
Kimeitek lands were affected by land alienation, especially in Kericho where tea plantations expanded.
Some clan members were displaced or forced into wage labor on European farms.
After independence:
The clan integrated into modern education, politics, and business.
Despite modernization, clan identity remains important in marriage, funerals, and community leadership.
7. Modern Identity
Today, the Kimeitek clan:
Is fully integrated within the Kipsigis community
Maintains strong respect for elders and clan lineage
Values education, land ownership, and unity
The clan continues to pass its history through oral narratives, proverbs, and family lineages.
Important Note (Honesty Part)
There is no single written authoritative document that records Kimeitek clan history in detail. What exists is oral history, passed down through generations. Variations in stories do not mean falsehood—they reflect migration paths and family branches.

S HUSSEIN VUMBI 0697006805

🔞

ILIYOPITA..
Moyo wangu uligonga kifua changu kwa nguvu.

Wote wapo.
Pamoja.
Na hawajuani.

"Wee kwani hujui kama ni mademu zangu au?"

Nilibaki nimezubaa, unajua mpaka nikahisi labda ninaota. Maana kuwaona Hainet na Farida sehemu moja sikutegemea.

Japo pia huu muunganiko ni waajabu kama vile kumuona Mama Mina na Madame Joy sehemu moja sio kitu cha kutegemea.

SONGA NAYO..
Nilibaki nashangaa shangaa pale, yaani wale watu wote walikuwa pale kwa sababu yangu. Nilihisi thamani ndani yangu, japo bado hofu ya kuwaona Hainet na Farida haikuniacha salama.

"Alhamdulillah umeamka tena mwanangu… hofu imetupungua.." alisema Mama Mina kwa sauti iliyotikiswa na hisia, akinishika mkono kana kwamba ningeweza kuyeyuka tena nikimuacha.

Nilitabasamu kwa tabu, nikavuta pumzi ndefu. Kichwa kilikuwa kizito kama nimebeba dunia nzima juu yake. Kabla hata sijazungumza, mmoja baada ya mwingine walinisogelea.. Mina, Dully, Roja, Choji, Madame Joy, Amara na Neema. Kila mmoja alikuwa na maneno yake ya pole, sala, utani mdogo wa kunipa nguvu. Chumba cha wodi kilijaa sauti za upendo na mshikamano.

Nilijisikia raha na amani kubwa moyoni mwangu. Kweli Mungu ana wakati wake, kwa maana mwezi mmoja tu nyuma nilikuwa naweza kushinda na njaa nikiwa peke yangu lakini sasa ninawatu ambao wanaacha kazi zao na kuja kwangu. Sio kama nina vya kuwapa ila wakati wa Mungu ni sahihi.

Hainet alikuja kukaa pembeni ya kitanda changu, karibu sana, uso wake ukiwa umejaa wasiwasi uliogeuzwa mahaba. Farida, kwa upande mwingine, alikuwa amesimama kidogo mbali, macho yake yakimtazama Hainet kwa jicho kali la ajabu, jicho la mwanamke anayesema mengi bila kufungua mdomo.

Hali ile iliwafanya waliokuwemo wodini wabaki wakitazamana kwa mshangao. Niliwaona wakijizuia kucheka, wengine wakificha tabasamu nyuma ya viganja vyao.

Hainet ndiye alianza kuzungumza. Alinishika mkono taratibu, sauti yake laini ikiniingia moja kwa moja moyoni.
"Umenitia hofu sana Ferra…  Nilihisi kama kuna kitu kibaya kimetokea. Nilikuwa naomba kila dakika."

"Ahsante.. Niko salama Hainet..!"

Farida akasonya, uso wake ukijaa wivu uliopambwa kwa uzuri wake ambao hauchoshi japo alikuwa na hasira. Alisogea karibu, aliniangalia machoni kwa namna ile ile anayoangalia mtu anayemiliki kitu chake.

"Na wewe, unaendeleaje?" Aliuliza kibabe lakini uzito wa mahaba yake haukijificha..
"Unajua ulivyonitisha?"

"Ahsante Farida.."

"Eti Fariidaa! Cheki bichwa lake bora ungekufaa..!" Farida aliongea huku anabana pua yake, lakini bado alikuwa kama kituko alituchekesha wote mule ndani.

"Wifi mdogo unataka kaka afe!!?" Mina alimuuliza Farida..

"We Mina.. Nitakuzibua bao la shingo uzimie siku 360..
Wifi mdogo ni shangazi yako...!" Alisema Farida tukabaki kucheka..

Wodini wote wakacheka. Ilikuwa ni ile kicheko cha watu wanaoona sinema ya moja kwa moja tamthilia isiyo na tiketi.

Mina akauliza swali zito, akikatiza ucheshi.
"Ferra, shida ilikuwa nini hasa?"

Nilimeza mate. Sikuthubutu kufungua ukurasa mzima wa kilichotokea. Nilichagua uwongo mmoja mfupi.
"Nilikuwa nafanya mazoezi… jogging. Ghafla mwili ukachoka sana, ndo nikapoteza fahamu!"

Dully akakunja uso kwa dhihaka ya kirafiki.
"Mazoezi mpaka nje ya mji, mashambani Mbasa?
Wakati safari yako ilibidi uje kwa Madame Joy!?"

Choji hakukosa neno.
"Labda alikuwa anakimbia akitaka kuona mwisho wa dunia!"

Kicheko kikapasuka tena wodini..

Waliponipa pole zote, niliuliza kwa mshangao, "Lakini mlijuaje nilipo?"

Mina akanieleza kwa utulivu.
"Tulipokuwa tunazungumza kwenye simu ulisema uko Mbasa, kwenye mashamba ya tangawizi. Halafu ghafla ukanyamaza. Tukapata hofu. Tulikuja kule kule, tukakukuta umelala huna fahamu. Ndipo tukakuleta hospital. Simu yako iliita, Hainet alipiga tukapokea tukamwambia. Farida naye alipiga, tukamwambia. Dully alipiga tukamueleza, naye akawajulisha wengine. Ndiyo maana wote tupo hapa."

Nilihisi kitu kizito kikishuka moyoni mwangu hisia ya kushukuriwa na kuwa na watu. Nikawatazama mmoja mmoja.
"Asanteni sana," nilisema kwa busara. "Ninathamini sana upendo wenu. Sio jambo dogo."

Dakika chache baadaye daktari akaingia. Alizungumza kitaalamu, kwa sauti tulivu ya mtu anayejua anachokisema.
"Ferra hana tatizo kubwa. Ametumia nguvu nyingi sana mwili umepoteza maji na nishati. Anatakiwa anywe maji mengi, ale vyakula vya kuongeza nguvu, matunda, asali, mayai, samaki, supu nzito. Kwa siku thelathini ajitunze."

Nilipumua kwa hafueni..

Ghafla Farida akamuita Hainet kwa sauti ya amri iliyojificha ndani ya hasira.
"We demu, njoo nje kidogo."

Hainet, akiwa mpole kama kawaida yake alisimama kwa hofu ndogo. Akatizama kama anatamani nisema jambo..

"Mtu yeyote asitufuate..!" Farida aliongeza kwa sauti iliyokatiza mawazo ya kila mtu.

Wote wakabaki kushangaa. Mimi moyo wangu ukadunda kwa kasi. Wakitoka nje, wodini ikawa kimya.

"Haya kaka.. Wale watu wa jangwani leo wamekutana.. Sikilizia ukame unaokuja!" Alisema Choji.

Roja akacheka.. "Hawa wawili wakiamua, hospital inaweza kugeuka uwanja wa vita. Ogopa mtu mpole kama Hainet na mtu anayependa bila maneno kama Farida..!"

"Uzuri ni kwamba... Hapa hapo ni hospital pamezoeleka damu!" Alisema Dully.

"Sasa kaka..
Which is which.. Hahaha..
Yaani yupi wifi na yupi sio?" Aliuliza Mina.

"Wote ni mawifi labda uliza yupo moja na yupi mbili..!?"

Madame Joy na Amara walizungumza kwa pamoja kana kwamba waliambizana, watu walikuwa wanafanya utani wakati Farida alionekana kutoka kishari.

"Nyie hamuwazi watu wameondoka kishari!!" Niliwauliza.

"Hamna shari mwanangu.. Nachoshukuru wewe ni rijali..
Wale wanawake wote wanakupenda, wewe ni muislam na wao wote waislam, nadhani umenielewa!" Alisema Mama Mina.

Baada ya muda walirudi. Cha kushangaza, Farida alikuwa kawaida kabisa, kana kwamba hakuna kilichotokea. Hainet alikuwa na tabasamu pana, la furaha ya mtu aliyeshinda mtihani mgumu. Wote tukabaki kuangaliana kwa mshangao.

Safari ikaanza kuondoka..

"We Ferra mbichwaa..
Leo nenda kwa huyo demu wako wakishua, kule Minazini hatutaki watu wanye bichwa kama lako.." Alisema Farida kama vile miye sio mpenzi wake.

Walipokubaliana kuwa siku ile ningeondoka na Hainet, wengine wakaagana na kuondoka zao. Nikaingia kwenye gari la Hainet, nikiwa bado na maumivu madogo lakini akili ikiwa sawa.

Tukiwa ndani ya gari safari ya kwenda kule kwa Mzee Karim, Hainet akavunja ukimya kwa kicheko.
"Yule mwanamke akili zake sio nzuri ujue."

Nikageuka kumtazama. "Kafanya nini?"

Akanicheka zaidi..
"Kaniambia niache shobo na nyumbani kwake. Kasema nisije pale kwako tena. Eti mimi ni tajiri nipange nyumba sehemu nyingine. Akasema nikija mtaani kwake namdhalilisha, kwa sababu mimi mzuri, yeye ataonekana kama katuni aliyechorwa na kichaa."

Tulicheka wote wawili, kicheko kikubwa.. Sikuelewa akili za Farida zipoje mi nikadhani utamtukana.

"Mimi nikamwambia mbona na yeye mzuri.." Hainet akaendelea. "Akasema hataki shobo.."

Kicheko kikarejea tena, kikachanganyika na upepo wa jioni uliokuwa ukiingia kupitia dirisha la gari.

Kisha sauti yake ikabadilika, ikawa nzito kidogo.
"Lakini kasema mambo ya maana… magumu kwa mwanamke kuyakubali. Kasema kwenye dunia ya sasa ni ngumu kumpata mwanaume wa peke yako. Lakini alisema alikuwa anakujali tangu zamani sana. Hakuweza kukubaliana na maisha yako ya wakati ule. Hakuwahi kukuona kama chokoraa wa kudumu, lakini hakuweza kukubadilisha, japo watu walikuona kama chokoraa yeye aliona ni dhahabu iliyochafuka kwa tope..
Kasema hawezi kunichukia wala kunikataza, kwa sababu anaona mimi ni daraja lako la kufikia ndoto zako, la kutoka kwenye maisha ya kudhalilika ambayo anaamini siyo yako."

Nilikaa kimya kwa sekunde chache, nikitafakari. Nilihisi mchanganyiko wa ucheshi, mahaba na hekima ya maisha. Dunia haikuwa nyeusi wala nyeupe ilikuwa na rangi nyingi kati.

"Mimi binafsi nilishakuelewa kuwa natambua una mpenzi wako..
Lakini ni maajabu ya Mungu mpenzi wako kakubali kuwa mimi ni mpenzi wako.."

Nikacheka kwanza.. Hainet akaendeleaa..

"Nadhani ni Mungu alipanga tuwe hivyo, naamini mioyo miwili inaweza kupenda moyo mmoja..!"

Nikamtazama Hainet, nikatabasamu kwa shukrani.
"Maisha yana walimu wengi.." nilisema taratibu kana kwamba nataka kuongea point. "Na wakati mwingine wanakuja wakiwa wanawake wawili ndani ya wodi moja."

Hainet akacheka, gari likazidi kusonga mbele, na mimi nikajua siku hiyo haikuwa tu ya kupona mwili ilikuwa ni somo la moyo.

Ile siku nililala na Hainet kwao pale kwenye nyumba mpya, maana hakukuwa na mtu wale ndugu zake aliosema wametoka Hanaka walikuwa wameenda kule kwenye nyumba yao nyingine ambayo ndipo familia yao inaishi.

Siku ile sikufanya chochote usiku, hamu sikuwa nayo kwakuwa nilikuwa nimefanya kwa fujo ya ajabu kwa Mke wa Magesa na Shangazi yake Aisha. 

Mama Selehe na Mama Nurat..

Nililala sana, nilikuja kuamshwa na Hainet..

"Mume wangu shika simu kuna mtu anataka kuzungumza na wewe!" Aliniambia Hainet kwa sauti tulivu akinipa simu.

Nilipokea simu nikaweka sikioni..

"We bichwa.. Huyo anakuita Mume wake umemuoa lini wewe!" Nilisikia sauti ya Farida, usingizi wote ukaisha.

"Kwani wewe ni Farida au Faina wa Naza!?" Nilimuuliza.

"Mimi bibi yako kwani vipi?" 

Nilibaki kucheka, huyu Farida ni mcharuko kweli kweli. Ndivyo alivyo ila ni kama alikuwa mtulivu baada ya kuingia kwenye penzi langu, ila ni kama kuonana na Hainet kumeboost alirudi kwenye ucharuko wake.

"Vipi lakini Mume Wangu mbichwa unaendeleaje?" Farida alipoa na kujulia hali.

"Nimeamka poa sana...!"

Tuliongea kidogo, kisha simu ilikatwa..

"Hujambo mume wangu..!" Aliniuliza Hainet huku alikaa juu ya kiuno changu.

"Kwahiyo unamkalia mgonjwa..!"

"Ndiyo si umesema hujambo?"

"Nimekwambia muda gani?"

"Umemwambia Farida.."

"Kwani wewe ni Farida..?"

"Ni kama Farida tu..!"

Hainet aliishia kunibusu, tango lilianza fujo lakini bado lilikuwa na maumivu.

"Oyaaa.. We bado unaumwaa acha kupenda Ngono utakufaa.." 
Ilikuwa sauti ya Choji..

Hapo nilianza kuwasikia Choji, Dully na Roja wakiwa wanapiga kelele zao mlangoni na kugonga mlango kwa fujo.

"Hawa wamekuja saa ngapi?" Nilimuuliza Hainet.

"Eeh tokea saa moja.."

Mida ilikuwa ni saa mbili, ikabidi nioge kisha nilitoka kunywa chai na kuonana na machizi wale.

Tulikunywa chai kwa pamoja huku nikiwaeleza kuwa tunaenda kazini kwa Madame Joy kumaliza kazi.

"Ungepumzika jamaa.. Doctor kasema ule vyakula wanavyokula wagonjwa wa zinaa ili upate nguvu!"

"Nini wewe..?" Nilimuuliza Choji ambaye aliropoka.

Tulibaki kucheka tu..

"Ukitoka unatoka na gari sawa, hutakiwi kuzurura kama kuku, halafu kwenye nyumba tunaenda lini sasa!" Alisema Hainet.

"Kwenye gari hapo ndio penyewe.." Wakina Dully walifurahi sana.

"Mmoja aende na Hainet kwenye nyumba wengine twende kazini, tupige kazi ili hilo gari tuweze kulimudu..!"

Suala la nyumba tulishazungumza usiku na Hainet hivyo halikuwa jipya kwangu, ilitakiwa tupate nyumba ya kuishi na Hainet tofauti na hapo kwao wala pale kwangu ambapo walikubaliana na Farida kuwa kule ni utawala wa Farida.

"Mimi nadhani twende pale kazini, tupe maelekezo.. 
Sisi tushakubaliana kwamba wewe ndiye boss wetu, kwa hiyo tupe maelekezo ya kazi kisha wewe uende na shem kutafuta nyumba.. Nyumba ya kuishi nyie sio vizuri atafute mtu mwingine.." Alisema Roja.

"Kweli Shem una akili wewe.." Hainet alimpongeza Roja.

Ni kweli niliona wazo lile ni zuri zaidi, nilikubaliana nao.

"We boya hatujakubaliana uwe boss.. Ila ni kiongozi wetu!!" Alisema Choji.

"Yaani we uwe boss wetu na pua lako hilo kama nyundo ya machimboni!" Aliongeza Dully.

Nilimuaga Hainet kwa mabusu mazito, kisha nilimtaka ajiendae nikirudi kutoka kazini twende kutafuta nyumba.

Siku ile ikawa hivyo, niliwapeleka wakina Choji nikawapa maelekezo, kisha nilirudi kwa Hainet tukaenda kutafuta nyumba.

Mpaka saa 10 jioni, tayari tulipata nyumba nzuri ambayo Hainet aliinunua kabisa, mida hiyo ya jioni tulikuwa tunapanga vitu ndani.

Nilianza Maisha mapya kabisa, nikiwa na Hainet na Farida..

Minazini niliishi na Farida na maisha yangu ya Minazini yaliendelea lakini yalikuwa ya uhakika tofauti na zamani.

Pia niliishi Funguni, ndio mtaa ambao tulipata nyumba mimi na Hainet.

Kiukweli Mungu alifungua sana njia, sikuwa tajiri, ila nilikuwa na uhakika wa maisha, sio kwa sababu ya Hainet ila ni kazi ambazo zilifunguka kupitia Mzee Karim na Madame Joy.

Tulikuwa tunapata sana kazi, kiasi cha kuwa busy mno mimi na wakina Dully. Hata pale mtaani kuonekana ilikuwa ni mara chache, au usiku tukirudi kutoka kazini. Mimi ndio kabisa nilikuwa adimu maana nilikuwa nina makazi mawili.

Roja aliachana na kazi ya bodaboda kujikita kwenye kazi yetu ya bustani na usafi wa majengo.

Ile nyumba ya Minazini nayo niliongeza vyumba viwili japo sio vya kifahari ila kidogo nyumba ilianza kuonekana..

Stori za mtaani zikiwa haaziishi, watu walijadili kuhusu kulelewa wakisema kuwa nimehongwa gari na mwanamke. Sikuwajali kabisa..

Siku zile zote Aisha sikuonana naye alikuwa busy na Ridhiwani wake kwa taarifa nilizopewa pale kijiweni kwa siku ambazo nilipata nafasi ya kukaa.

Mama Mina na Mina walikuwa wanafanya biashara ya kuku kwa ile pesa ambayo Hainet aliwapa.

Unaweza kudhani tunamaliza eeeh.. Bado..

Siku ile ilikuwa imeanza vizuri baada ya kutoka kwenye kazi tuliyopata kufanya bustani kwenye hotel moja kubwa mjini Saya..

Nilikuwa ndani ya gari nikirudi Minazini, nilikuwa peke yangu maana wakina Dully wao kila mmoja alienda na safari zake. Walikuwa na hela za hivyo misele ni mingi sana, hamu ya gari pia iliwaisha baada ya kulifaidi kwa miezi mitatu..

Taratibu nilikuwa natazama mitaa ya Minazini nikiwa natembeza Mercedes Benz taratibu gari ambalo nilipewa na Hainet kwa matumizi.
Mitaa ambayo nilikuwa nadharaulika miezi kadhaa nyuma, ila kwa kipindi hicho kuna watu walikuwa wanatamani maisha yangu.

Mitaa ambayo hapo zamani lilikuwa eneo la Babu yangu Mzee Vumbi kabla ya kuuzwa uzwa sana.

Nilikuwa naweza kuweka mafuta kwenye gari sasa, kutoka kwenda kushindwa mlo mmoja, nilikuwa nasimamishwa kusalimiwa kutoka kwenye kuchuniwa salamu.

Nikiwa karabia nyumbani simu yangu ikaingia ujumbe..

'Mimi ni Mama Selehe mke wa Magesa..
Kwenye simu yangu kuna video ya lile tulio ulilofanya siku ile..
Pale kulikuwa na kamera za siri, sasa basi, uje uwanja wa Juhudi hapa..
Nikueleza nachohitaji au hizi video nizisambaze mitandaoni na kwa wanawake zakooo.. Unajua nini kitatokea kwa Farida ambaye ana mimba..
