Cousin’s ER surgeon date mocked my "fake" career—until she saw my trauma certification...

The wine glass in my hand was shaking.

Not from nerves.

From fourteen straight hours in the trauma bay at Memorial Hospital—three code blues, two gunshot wounds, and one pediatric drowning I’d helped pull back from the edge.

My hands were steady when they needed to be. When a kid’s airway closed or someone’s blood pressure crashed, I could move like a machine and think like a chess player at the same time.

But here, in my parents’ living room on Christmas Eve, surrounded by tinsel and relatives who treated medicine like a status contest, my body finally admitted what my brain refused to: I was exhausted.

Across the room, my cousin Derek looked relaxed. Fresh haircut. Crisp sweater. That grin he always wore when he was about to take a jab and watch it land.

His arm was hooked around a woman in a designer dress with perfect hair and the kind of posture that screamed, I’m used to being admired.

“This is Natasha,” Derek announced loudly, like he was presenting a prize. “She’s a real doctor. ER surgeon at Boston General. Not like some people.”

He looked straight at me when he said it.

The room laughed—polite, nervous little chuckles. The kind people make when they’re afraid of rocking the boat.

Natasha’s mouth curled into a smile that didn’t reach her eyes. “Nice to meet you,” she said, extending her hand.

I shook it. Firm. Professional.

“James,” I said. “Registered nurse. Trauma unit at Memorial in Philly.”

“Oh,” she said. “Nursing.”

She said it like someone saying, Oh. You work in customer service.

Derek’s grin widened. “Yeah, he’s our little hospital hero. Takes vitals, hands out blankets. You know.”

My jaw tightened. I kept my face neutral. Years in emergency medicine teach you how to swallow reactions.

But the old part of me—the kid who used to play basketball with Derek in my uncle’s driveway—felt something twist. Not sadness.

Betrayal.

Because Derek knew better.

Or at least… he should have.

When We Were Kids, We Were Brothers

Growing up, Derek and I were close.

Only children. Same neighborhood. Parents who were siblings. Summers that smelled like sunburn and cut grass. We fought, made up, fought again.

We even dreamed the same dream.

Medicine.

Back then it wasn’t about titles or hierarchy. It was about helping. Being the person who knew what to do.

When I told everyone I wanted to be a nurse, I meant it. I wanted direct patient care, the kind of work where your hands could change outcomes. I liked the team part of it. The speed. The reality.

Derek wanted the letters.

MD.

And once he got into med school, everything changed.

His parents threw him a party like he’d been elected president. My aunt cried. My uncle made a toast about Derek being “the pride of the family.”

When I told my parents I’d gotten into nursing school, my mom smiled politely and asked, “Have you thought about medical school instead?”

When I explained nursing was what I wanted, she patted my hand and said, “Well… someone has to do it.”

That sentence planted itself in me like a splinter.

From then on, it got worse.

Derek joked about whether I “got my degree online.”

My uncle asked why I’d “waste intelligence” on a job that didn’t require a “real education.”

Aunts asked when I’d “go back for something better.”

At first I tried to explain.

Trauma nursing wasn’t fluff. It wasn’t “fetching supplies.” It was rapid assessment, airway management, titrating drips, coordinating with surgeons, running protocols, making decisions so fast you didn’t realize you’d made them until you were already executing them.

But every time I talked, they nodded politely and changed the subject.

And Derek? Derek kept score.

Second year of med school, he started calling me after hard days.

Not to bond.

To establish hierarchy.

“It’s brutal,” he’d say. “But I guess it’s different for nurses. You just follow orders, right?”

If I corrected him, he laughed.

“Relax. I’m not saying nursing isn’t important. It’s just… not the same level of responsibility.”

Then he finished residency and took an emergency medicine job in Boston, and suddenly every family gathering became his stage.

Thanksgiving two years ago: he explained a case like he was giving grand rounds, then turned to me and asked, “Do you even understand what I’m talking about? I know nursing school doesn’t really cover pathophysiology.”

I’d been trauma-certified for years by then. Could’ve run circles around him on airway and hemorrhage control, but I just said, “I understand enough.”

Christmas last year: he brought a different physician girlfriend. They made inside jokes about medical terminology and laughed when I asked them to clarify.

“It’s a medical school thing,” Derek said. “You probably didn’t cover it.”

I had.

I’d taught it.

But I stopped trying.

Because in my family, credibility wasn’t about competence.

It was about titles...

Confessions of a Passenger Princess : Midwest Snow Edition 

If you see my husband’s Jeep crawling through Fort Wayne today at the speed of a determined snail, please know this: it’s not broken. It’s just me. I’m from the South, where if a single snowflake sneezes in our general direction, we shut the town down, buy all the milk and bread, and emotionally prepare for the end times. Meanwhile, the Midwest is out here like, “Oh, this? This is just weather.” I’m gripping the wheel of my husband’s brand-new Jeep Gladiator like it’s a life raft, whispering affirmations to it. There is no way I’m about to be the headline that reads, “Woman Destroys Husband’s Dream Vehicle Because She Thought She Could Handle Winter.”

Every stoplight is a negotiation. Every turn is taken with the grace of a confused parade float. People are passing me, waving kindly—or maybe aggressively, it’s hard to tell through the frost—but I’m focused. Focused on not sliding. Focused on not panicking. Focused on the sacred vow I made to myself: I will not wreck this Jeep. Not today. Not ever.

I firmly believe cars drive better when someone else is behind the wheel.

I miss my natural habitat: the passenger seat, where I offer moral support, playlist control, and unhelpful navigation tips.

I trust my husband completely… which is exactly why I should not be driving his truck in Midwest winter weather.

So if you’re stuck behind me, just know I’m doing my best. I’ll get there eventually. Slowly. Safely. Like a Southern girl in a Jeep, discovering that snow is not a suggestion—it’s a lifestyle. ❄️🚗

Akasema:

“Usihuzunike; kwa hakika haya ndiyo aliyoniachia bishara Mtume wa Allah (s.a.w) siku moja.”

“Nilikuwa mimi na fulani na fulani na fulani  akawataja kwa majina yao — Mtume (s.a.w) akaingia kwetu akasema:

Creamed Chipped Beef on Toast

(serves 4)

You want easy? THIS is easy! A lot of people tease me because of this recipe. But I don't care. It tastes great on a chilly afternoon and is extremely simple to make. Call it what you will...but the ol' S.O.S. is staying in my recipe files!

Ingredients~

2 Tablespoons of butter

2 Tablespoons of flour

2 cups of milk

2 4-ounce packages of dried beef (like Buddig)

Salt and pepper to taste

Bread for toast

Directions~

In a saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat.

Stir in the flour until smooth. Heat until it bubbles slightly.

Slowly stir in the milk.

Stir to keep from getting lumpy. The white sauce will thicken as it cooks.

Cut the beef into small pieces and add to the white sauce.

Turn the heat to low and continue stirring for 5 minutes.

Toast bread slices.

Place toast on a plate and top with a portion of the white sauce.

"MY HUSKY WAS HIDING IN THE DRYER WHILE THE COPS WERE HERE. I THOUGHT HE WAS SCARED—UNTIL HE DROPPED THE ONE THING THAT PROVED MY ENTIRE LIFE WAS A LIE.

The dryer was still warm when I found him.

My 80-pound Siberian Husky, Cooper, was crammed into the drum like a discarded sweater, his blue eyes blown wide with a terror I didn't understand.

""Elena? Is everything alright in there?""

Detective Miller’s voice drifted from the kitchen, smooth and polished like a river stone. He had been coming by every day since Marcus died. To ""check on me."" To ""update me on the investigation.""

I thought he was my lifeline. I thought the police were the only thing standing between me and whatever darkness had taken my husband.

""I'm fine!"" I shouted back, my voice cracking. ""Cooper is just... he's acting weird.""

I reached into the dryer, my hands shaking as I grabbed Cooper’s collar to pull him out. He wasn't just hiding; he was vibrating. His fur was matted with sweat, and his ears were pinned so far back they almost disappeared.

""Come on, boy. It’s just Miller. He’s a friend, remember?""

But Cooper didn't move. He looked past me, toward the kitchen door where the shadow of the detective loomed. Then, with a desperate, guttural whine, he nudged his head against my palm.

Something hard and cold hit the floor.

Clink.

It was small. Smaller than a dime. A matte black disc with a tiny, rhythmic blinking red light.

It hadn't fallen from the dryer. It had fallen from Cooper’s fur. Specifically, from the underside of his heavy leather collar—the one Marcus had bought him the day before the ""accident.""

My heart didn't just skip a beat; it stopped.

I looked at the device. Then I looked at the shadow in the doorway.

The light on the device flickered—once, twice—confirming it was active. Transmitting.

Every scream, every private sob, every phone call I’d made to my lawyer, every secret Marcus had whispered to me before he left that final morning... they had heard it all.

And the man who had been ""protecting"" me was the one holding the receiver.

""Elena?"" The floorboards creaked. Miller was moving toward the laundry room. ""Why is it so quiet in there?""

I looked at Cooper. His eyes were fixed on the door, his teeth bared in a silent snarl.

That was the moment I realized: My husband didn't die in an accident. And if I didn't act in the next ten seconds, I wasn't going to make it out of this house alive.

Chapter 1: The Cold Metal of Truth
The air in the suburbs of Oak Ridge, Virginia, always smelled like freshly cut grass and false security. It was the kind of neighborhood where people didn't lock their doors until the sun went down, and where the police were people you invited over for barbecue.

But since Marcus died, the air in our house had turned sour. It smelled like stale coffee, unwashed laundry, and the heavy, metallic scent of grief.

I was standing in the middle of the laundry room, the hum of the refrigerator the only sound in the house, until the floorboards groaned in the hallway.

""You haven't touched your tea, Elena,"" Detective Ryan Miller said, leaning against the doorframe.

Miller was the picture of a ""good cop."" He had that salt-and-pepper hair that suggested wisdom, and a pair of empathetic brown eyes that made you want to spill your guts. He’d been Marcus’s best friend on the force. When the paramedics pulled Marcus’s crushed Tesla out of the ravine three weeks ago, Miller was the one who held me while I screamed.

""I'm not hungry, Ryan. Or thirsty,"" I said, not looking at him.

""You have to maintain your strength. The department is doing everything we can to find out why the brakes failed, but I need you sharp. If you remember anything else Marcus said about the 'project' he was working on at the firm...""

I didn't answer. I was looking for Cooper. Usually, the Husky was my shadow, but for the last hour, he’d been missing.

""Cooper?"" I called out.

Silence.

""Maybe he slipped out back?"" Miller suggested, his voice low and soothing. Too soothing.

I walked past him, feeling a strange shiver as our shoulders brushed. There was something about Miller today—a tension in his jaw, a way his eyes kept scanning my face as if looking for a crack in a mask.

I checked the living room. Nothing. I checked the basement stairs. Nothing.

Then I heard it. A faint, rhythmic thumping.

It was coming from the laundry room I had just left.

I doubled back. Miller followed, his boots heavy on the hardwood. I stopped in front of the stackable dryer. The door was slightly ajar.

I pulled it open, and my breath hitched.

Cooper was wedged inside, his massive frame curled into a ball of white and grey fur. He was hyperventilating, his tongue lolling out, his eyes darting toward Miller and then back to me.

""Oh, baby,"" I whispered, reaching in. ""What are you doing in there? Was it the thunder?""

There hadn't been any thunder. It was a clear, scorching Tuesday.

""He's probably just stressed,"" Miller said from behind me. He reached out a hand to pat Cooper’s head, but the dog did something he had never done in his five years of life.

He snapped.

His teeth grazed Miller’s glove, a low, demonic growl vibrating in his chest.

Miller flinched back, his face darkening. ""Whoa. Easy there, big guy.""

""He’s never done that,"" I said, my heart hammering. ""Ryan, I think something’s wrong with him.""

I grabbed Cooper by the scruff, trying to coax him out of the drum. He resisted at first, his claws scratching against the metal, but then he saw the look in my eyes—the pure, unadulterated fear—and he relented. He practically fell out of the dryer, landing on the floor with a heavy thud.

He didn't run. He didn't lick my face.

He stood between me and Miller, his hackles raised. Then, he ducked his head and rubbed his neck vigorously against my shin, as if trying to scratch an itch he couldn't reach.

That’s when it fell.

A tiny, black plastic disc. It bounced once on the linoleum and rolled to a stop right between my feet.

I stared at it. It looked like a button, or a piece of a toy. But then the light hit it, and I saw the microscopic lens and the pulsing crimson glow of a 'Record' light.

The world went silent.

I remembered Marcus bought that collar. He had insisted on it. “It’s top-of-the-line, El. Built-in GPS. In case he gets lost while I’m at the office.”

But this wasn't a GPS tracker.

I looked up at Miller. He wasn't looking at the dog anymore. He was looking at the floor. At the device.

The ""empathetic"" look in his eyes vanished, replaced by a cold, calculating stillness that made my blood turn to ice.

""You should have left him in the dryer, Elena,"" Miller whispered.

He reached for the radio on his shoulder, his thumb hovering over the button.

""Get back,"" I gasped, grabbing Cooper’s collar.

""Give it to me,"" Miller said, taking a step forward. His hand moved from his radio to the snap on his holster. ""Give me the device, and we can talk about this. I loved Marcus, Elena. I don't want to hurt his widow.""

""You loved him?"" My voice was a jagged shard of glass. ""You were listening to us. You were listening to him for weeks! Did you hear him cry out when you cut those brake lines, Ryan? Did you listen to his last breath?""

The silence that followed was the loudest thing I’d ever heard.

Miller didn't deny it. He just sighed, a weary, frustrated sound. ""Marcus was an idiot. He thought he could whistleblow on the entire precinct and walk away clean. He thought he was a hero. And you... you just couldn't stop asking questions, could you?""

Outside, a car door slammed. Then another.

Two more police cruisers pulled into my driveway, their blue and red lights silent but blinding as they reflected off the kitchen windows.

I wasn't being protected. I was being surrounded.

Cooper let out a bark that shook the walls, his body tensed for a spring. I looked at the back door, then back at Miller, who now had his glock drawn, pointed at the floor, but ready.

""Don't make this a tragedy, Elena,"" he said. ""Just hand over the bug.""

I realized then that the device didn't just have our conversations. It had his voice. It probably had the recording of whoever had been on the other end of that transmission.

It was the only thing that could prove Marcus was murdered.

I didn't hand it over. I lunged for the back door, screaming for Cooper to run.

The glass of the kitchen window shattered as a bullet whistled past my ear, and the nightmare began."

"MY HUSKY WAS HIDING IN THE DRYER WHILE THE COPS WERE HERE. I THOUGHT HE WAS SCARED—UNTIL HE DROPPED THE ONE THING THAT PROVED MY ENTIRE LIFE WAS A LIE.

The dryer was still warm when I found him.

My 80-pound Siberian Husky, Cooper, was crammed into the drum like a discarded sweater, his blue eyes blown wide with a terror I didn't understand.

""Elena? Is everything alright in there?""

Detective Miller’s voice drifted from the kitchen, smooth and polished like a river stone. He had been coming by every day since Marcus died. To ""check on me."" To ""update me on the investigation.""

I thought he was my lifeline. I thought the police were the only thing standing between me and whatever darkness had taken my husband.

""I'm fine!"" I shouted back, my voice cracking. ""Cooper is just... he's acting weird.""

I reached into the dryer, my hands shaking as I grabbed Cooper’s collar to pull him out. He wasn't just hiding; he was vibrating. His fur was matted with sweat, and his ears were pinned so far back they almost disappeared.

""Come on, boy. It’s just Miller. He’s a friend, remember?""

But Cooper didn't move. He looked past me, toward the kitchen door where the shadow of the detective loomed. Then, with a desperate, guttural whine, he nudged his head against my palm.

Something hard and cold hit the floor.

Clink.

It was small. Smaller than a dime. A matte black disc with a tiny, rhythmic blinking red light.

It hadn't fallen from the dryer. It had fallen from Cooper’s fur. Specifically, from the underside of his heavy leather collar—the one Marcus had bought him the day before the ""accident.""

My heart didn't just skip a beat; it stopped.

I looked at the device. Then I looked at the shadow in the doorway.

The light on the device flickered—once, twice—confirming it was active. Transmitting.

Every scream, every private sob, every phone call I’d made to my lawyer, every secret Marcus had whispered to me before he left that final morning... they had heard it all.

And the man who had been ""protecting"" me was the one holding the receiver.

""Elena?"" The floorboards creaked. Miller was moving toward the laundry room. ""Why is it so quiet in there?""

I looked at Cooper. His eyes were fixed on the door, his teeth bared in a silent snarl.

That was the moment I realized: My husband didn't die in an accident. And if I didn't act in the next ten seconds, I wasn't going to make it out of this house alive.

Chapter 1: The Cold Metal of Truth
The air in the suburbs of Oak Ridge, Virginia, always smelled like freshly cut grass and false security. It was the kind of neighborhood where people didn't lock their doors until the sun went down, and where the police were people you invited over for barbecue.

But since Marcus died, the air in our house had turned sour. It smelled like stale coffee, unwashed laundry, and the heavy, metallic scent of grief.

I was standing in the middle of the laundry room, the hum of the refrigerator the only sound in the house, until the floorboards groaned in the hallway.

""You haven't touched your tea, Elena,"" Detective Ryan Miller said, leaning against the doorframe.

Miller was the picture of a ""good cop."" He had that salt-and-pepper hair that suggested wisdom, and a pair of empathetic brown eyes that made you want to spill your guts. He’d been Marcus’s best friend on the force. When the paramedics pulled Marcus’s crushed Tesla out of the ravine three weeks ago, Miller was the one who held me while I screamed.

""I'm not hungry, Ryan. Or thirsty,"" I said, not looking at him.

""You have to maintain your strength. The department is doing everything we can to find out why the brakes failed, but I need you sharp. If you remember anything else Marcus said about the 'project' he was working on at the firm...""

I didn't answer. I was looking for Cooper. Usually, the Husky was my shadow, but for the last hour, he’d been missing.

""Cooper?"" I called out.

Silence.

""Maybe he slipped out back?"" Miller suggested, his voice low and soothing. Too soothing.

I walked past him, feeling a strange shiver as our shoulders brushed. There was something about Miller today—a tension in his jaw, a way his eyes kept scanning my face as if looking for a crack in a mask.

I checked the living room. Nothing. I checked the basement stairs. Nothing.

Then I heard it. A faint, rhythmic thumping.

It was coming from the laundry room I had just left.

I doubled back. Miller followed, his boots heavy on the hardwood. I stopped in front of the stackable dryer. The door was slightly ajar.

I pulled it open, and my breath hitched.

Cooper was wedged inside, his massive frame curled into a ball of white and grey fur. He was hyperventilating, his tongue lolling out, his eyes darting toward Miller and then back to me.

""Oh, baby,"" I whispered, reaching in. ""What are you doing in there? Was it the thunder?""

There hadn't been any thunder. It was a clear, scorching Tuesday.

""He's probably just stressed,"" Miller said from behind me. He reached out a hand to pat Cooper’s head, but the dog did something he had never done in his five years of life.

He snapped.

His teeth grazed Miller’s glove, a low, demonic growl vibrating in his chest.

Miller flinched back, his face darkening. ""Whoa. Easy there, big guy.""

""He’s never done that,"" I said, my heart hammering. ""Ryan, I think something’s wrong with him.""

I grabbed Cooper by the scruff, trying to coax him out of the drum. He resisted at first, his claws scratching against the metal, but then he saw the look in my eyes—the pure, unadulterated fear—and he relented. He practically fell out of the dryer, landing on the floor with a heavy thud.

He didn't run. He didn't lick my face.

He stood between me and Miller, his hackles raised. Then, he ducked his head and rubbed his neck vigorously against my shin, as if trying to scratch an itch he couldn't reach.

That’s when it fell.

A tiny, black plastic disc. It bounced once on the linoleum and rolled to a stop right between my feet.

I stared at it. It looked like a button, or a piece of a toy. But then the light hit it, and I saw the microscopic lens and the pulsing crimson glow of a 'Record' light.

The world went silent.

I remembered Marcus bought that collar. He had insisted on it. “It’s top-of-the-line, El. Built-in GPS. In case he gets lost while I’m at the office.”

But this wasn't a GPS tracker.

I looked up at Miller. He wasn't looking at the dog anymore. He was looking at the floor. At the device.

The ""empathetic"" look in his eyes vanished, replaced by a cold, calculating stillness that made my blood turn to ice.

""You should have left him in the dryer, Elena,"" Miller whispered.

He reached for the radio on his shoulder, his thumb hovering over the button.

""Get back,"" I gasped, grabbing Cooper’s collar.

""Give it to me,"" Miller said, taking a step forward. His hand moved from his radio to the snap on his holster. ""Give me the device, and we can talk about this. I loved Marcus, Elena. I don't want to hurt his widow.""

""You loved him?"" My voice was a jagged shard of glass. ""You were listening to us. You were listening to him for weeks! Did you hear him cry out when you cut those brake lines, Ryan? Did you listen to his last breath?""

The silence that followed was the loudest thing I’d ever heard.

Miller didn't deny it. He just sighed, a weary, frustrated sound. ""Marcus was an idiot. He thought he could whistleblow on the entire precinct and walk away clean. He thought he was a hero. And you... you just couldn't stop asking questions, could you?""

Outside, a car door slammed. Then another.

Two more police cruisers pulled into my driveway, their blue and red lights silent but blinding as they reflected off the kitchen windows.

I wasn't being protected. I was being surrounded.

Cooper let out a bark that shook the walls, his body tensed for a spring. I looked at the back door, then back at Miller, who now had his glock drawn, pointed at the floor, but ready.

""Don't make this a tragedy, Elena,"" he said. ""Just hand over the bug.""

I realized then that the device didn't just have our conversations. It had his voice. It probably had the recording of whoever had been on the other end of that transmission.

It was the only thing that could prove Marcus was murdered.

I didn't hand it over. I lunged for the back door, screaming for Cooper to run.

The glass of the kitchen window shattered as a bullet whistled past my ear, and the nightmare began."

Today is a very important day in Sanatan Dharma, with many communities celebrating the end of winter as the earth changes position on it's axis and the Sun enters Makar Rashi 

This day is celebrated throughout Bharat, and in Gujrat & Rajastan, it is known as Uttarayan. It is a highly auspicious day, and people make Tal na Ladva (sweet laddus made from sesame seeds) and fly kites to celebrate

During the Mahabharat war, Bhishma had a boon that he could choose when to die, and decided to die on Makar Sankranti because of the positivity this day brings in the world

The Tamil community also celebrate Pongal on this day by boiling rice with milk and jaggery together, and people let the milk spill over the pot as an auspicious sign of abundance and prosperity. This sweet dish, known as Pongal, is offered to the Sun as a gratitude for good harvesting and later distributed as prasad

Do you celebrate on any other ways? Let us know in the comments - we'd love to hear it!

Mimi ni Mtanzania na niko hapa Marekani. Vurugu hizi zinazoshuhudiwa Marekani zilianza kushamiri katika mji wa Minneapolis, ambao uko karibu na ninapoishi.
Kinachoendelea hapa Marekani ni tofauti na kile unachoelezea. Tatizo kubwa ni kwamba serikali ya shirikisho imeleta askari wa uhamiaji (ICE), ambao wanapita mitaani na maeneo mbalimbali kwa nguvu, wakiwakamata watu wanaodhaniwa kuwa hawana vibali halali vya kuishi nchini Marekani. Hatua hizi zimezua upinzani mkubwa miongoni mwa raia, wanaopinga ubabe na ukatili wa ICE. Jazba zimekuwa kubwa, na hali hiyo ndiyo inayosababisha vurugu unazoziona.

Kuandamana kwa amani kunatambuliwa na kuheshimiwa kama haki ya kikatiba ya Wamarekani. Raia wanaweza kukusanyika na kuandamana kulaani vitendo vya maafisa wa ICE, mradi wafanye hivyo kwa amani. Hakuna polisi atakayewazuia; badala yake, polisi wapo kulinda waandamanaji ili waweze kutekeleza haki yao ya kuandamana na kuikosoa serikali kwa amani.

Iwapo kutakuwa na Wamarekani wanaounga mkono ICE nao wakaandamana kwa amani, polisi pia watakuwepo kulinda usalama na kudumisha amani ya maandamano hayo.

Katika vurugu hizi unazoziona Marekani, hutawaona polisi wakitumia risasi na kuua watu ovyo. Ikitokea tukio la mauaji, kama ilivyotokea Minneapolis, hufanyiwa uchunguzi wa kina hadi mhusika apatikane na kufikishwa mahakamani. Tayari askari wa ICE anayesemekana kuhusika na tukio la mauaji ametambuliwa, na taratibu za kisheria zinaanza kuchukuliwa dhidi yake. Haki itatendeka.

Ni muhimu kutambua kuwa kuna tofauti kati ya askari wa ICE na polisi wa kawaida. Polisi wa Marekani hawana mamlaka ya kuingilia masuala ya uhamiaji. Hawahusiki na kifo cha mtu aliyeuawa Minneapolis. Chanzo cha mvutano ni namna askari wa ICE wanavyotekeleza majukumu yao kwa nguvu na kuwachochea raia hasira.

Meaning And Symbolism In The Boiling Over Of Milk In Pongal Festival
Pongal is a harvest festival celebrated in South India, particularly in Tamil Nadu, to mark the end of the winter solstice and the beginning of the harvest season. One of the key rituals during the Pongal festival is the preparation of a dish called "Pongal," which is a sweet rice dish made with newly harvested rice, jaggery (a type of unrefined sugar), and milk. The boiling over of milk during the preparation of Pongal holds special significance and symbolism in the festival. It is considered an auspicious sign, symbolizing prosperity and abundance. Here's a breakdown of the meaning and symbolism associated with the boiling over of milk during Pongal:
Overflowing Abundance: The act of allowing the milk to boil over the pot represents the abundance of the harvest and the prosperity that it brings. It is seen as a sign of good fortune and plenty in the coming year.
Symbol of Blessings: The overflowing milk is considered a symbol of divine blessings and fertility. It is believed to bring good luck to the household and the agricultural endeavors for the upcoming season.
Expressing Gratitude to Cattle: Pongal is not only a celebration of the harvest but also an occasion to express gratitude to cattle for their contribution to agriculture. The milk used in the preparation of Pongal is often sourced from cows, and the overflowing milk is seen as a way of honoring and thanking these animals.
Joy and Celebration: The act of allowing the milk to boil over is accompanied by joyous celebrations, with people shouting "Pongalo Pongal!" which translates to "Pongal overflows!" This adds to the festive atmosphere and the overall positive energy associated with the occasion.
Renewal and Growth: The Pongal festival marks a time of renewal and growth in nature, as it signifies the beginning of the harvest season. The boiling over of milk symbolizes the potential for growth, prosperity, and the fulfillment of aspirations in the coming year.
In essence, the boiling over of milk in the Pongal festival is a ritualistic and symbolic act that embodies the spirit of abundance, gratitude, and hope for a prosperous future. It is a beautiful tradition that connects the agricultural practices of the region with spiritual and cultural values.

HAY MAKING: EXACT STEPS TO PRODUCE HIGH-QUALITY FEED 🌾🐄

Many farmers lose money not because they lack grass, but because they make poor-quality hay. Moldy, dusty, or over-dry hay has low nutrients and causes livestock health problems. Good hay making is about timing, handling, and storage.
1️⃣ Choose the Right Grass • Napier, Rhodes grass, Brachiaria, Lucerne, or Sudan grass
• Grass should be leafy, not woody
• Avoid overgrown pasture
2️⃣ Correct Cutting Time (Very Important) • Cut grass at early flowering stage
• Too young → low yield
• Too old → low nutrients & hard stems
3️⃣ Best Time to Cut • Cut on a sunny, dry day
• Avoid rainy or cloudy periods
• Morning cutting is ideal after dew dries
4️⃣ Proper Drying • Spread grass thinly for uniform drying
• Turn hay 1–2 times daily
• Dry until moisture is about 15–20%
⚠️ Over-drying causes leaf loss (nutrients lost)
5️⃣ How to Know Hay Is Ready • Stems break, not bend
• Leaves remain green (not brown)
• No dampness inside bundles
6️⃣ Baling or Bundling • Bale or bundle only when fully dry
• Tight but not too compact
• Loose bales encourage air circulation
7️⃣ Storage • Store in a dry, well-ventilated shed
• Raise hay off the ground using pallets
• Protect from rain, termites, and rodents
8️⃣ Common Mistakes to Avoid ❌ Cutting grass too late
❌ Drying on bare soil
❌ Storing damp hay
❌ Leaving hay exposed to rain
9️⃣ Benefits of Good Hay • High milk and meat production
• Reduced feed costs
• Reliable feed during dry seasons

"The Neighborhood “Outcast” Just Lifted a 5,000lb SUV With His Bare Hands to Save My Daughter.

FULL STORY:

CHAPTER 1

I’ve lived in this cul-de-sac for twenty years. You know the type. It’s one of those cookie-cutter American suburbs where the grass is always cut to exactly two inches, the flags are out by Memorial Day, and the biggest scandal we usually deal with is someone leaving their trash cans on the curb a day too long.

I thought I knew everyone. I thought I had the whole street figured out. I’m Mark. I’m a creature of habit—fifty-five, bad knees, and a tendency to sit in my garage judging people I don’t understand. I’m not proud of it, but it’s the truth. And for the last six months, I’ve been judging the Miller family. specifically, their son, Liam.

The Millers are nice enough folks—quiet, polite, the kind of people who bring you cookies when they move in. But Liam… everyone whispered about Liam. He’s sixteen, big for his age—over six feet tall with broad shoulders—but he seemed completely vacant.

He is autistic and non-verbal. He spent his days sitting on their front porch in an old wooden rocking chair, wearing massive, battered noise-canceling headphones. He would just rock. Back and forth. Back and forth. Rhythmically. Endlessly.

He never made eye contact. He never waved back. If you said ""Good morning,"" he’d stare right through you like you were made of glass. To be honest, and it makes me sick to admit this now, he made people uncomfortable. I saw the way the other neighbors would cross the street to avoid walking past his house. I saw the local kids ride their bikes a little faster when they passed him, whispering ""weirdo"" or ""ghost.""

We didn’t know him. We didn’t try to know him. We just saw the headphones and the rocking and decided he wasn’t part of our world. We labeled him the ""outcast"" and moved on with our perfect little lives.

Then there was the Gable family across the street. The total opposite. Young, vibrant, loud in the best way possible. They had a little girl, Bella. Two years old. A literal ray of sunshine. Curly blonde hair, huge blue eyes, always running, always laughing. Bella was the heartbeat of the block. If Liam was the ghost, Bella was the life. She’d waddle down the driveway waving at everyone, even Liam. Liam never waved back, of course. He’d just keep rocking, lost in whatever world existed between his ears.

I sat there drinking my iced tea on many afternoons, thinking I was the pillar of the community, while the real strength was sitting right next door, silent and misunderstood. I didn’t know that everything I believed was about to be shattered in the span of ten terrifying seconds.

It was a Tuesday. A hot, humid Tuesday in July. The air was thick enough to chew on, the kind of heat that makes the asphalt shimmer and smell like tar. I was in my garage, tinkering with my old Ford, trying to get the alternator to behave. The garage door was open, so I had a front-row seat to the street.

I could see Liam on his porch, doing his rhythmic rocking. I could see Sarah Gable, Bella’s mom, in her driveway. She was unloading groceries from her massive, silver SUV. It was a beast of a car—one of those reinforced luxury tanks designed for off-roading, fully loaded with camping gear and groceries.

This is where the nightmare started. It happens so fast. You always hear people say that—""it happened in slow motion""—but that’s a lie. Accidents don’t happen in slow motion. They happen in a violent, chaotic blur that your brain can’t process until it’s too late.

Sarah had the trunk open. She was grabbing bags, rushing because the heat was melting the ice cream. Bella, being two, was darting around the driveway, chasing a butterfly or a leaf, just being a toddler. I watched Sarah turn to carry a heavy load into the house. She left the trunk open. She left Bella outside. It’s a mistake any parent could make. Just for ten seconds. Just to put the milk in the fridge.

But the driveway… the Gables have this steep, inclined driveway. And something was wrong with that SUV. Maybe the parking brake wasn’t fully engaged. Maybe the transmission pin slipped. I don’t know the mechanics of the failure; I just know the physics of the tragedy.

I heard a pop. A mechanical groan that sounded like a gunshot in the quiet afternoon.

I looked up from my workbench. The massive SUV, fully loaded, started to roll backward.

It wasn’t moving fast at first. Just a creep. But gravity is cruel. It picked up speed instantly. And Bella… oh god, Bella was right behind the rear tire. She was sitting on the concrete, playing with the Velcro on her shoe. She was so small. The car was so big.

I dropped my wrench. The sound of it hitting the concrete echoed, but it wasn’t loud enough to warn anyone. I screamed, ""SARAH! THE CAR!""

My voice tore through the humid air. But Sarah was inside.

Bella looked up. She didn’t understand. She saw the big shiny car moving and she didn’t know it was death coming for her. She didn’t move. She just stared, her little mouth opening in confusion.

I started running. I’m fifty-five years old with bad knees and a bad back. I knew, even as I sprinted down my driveway, that I wasn’t going to make it. I was fifty feet away. The car was five feet from her.

I watched in horror as the plastic bumper hit her. It knocked her flat onto her back. She didn’t even have time to cry out. And then, the rear tire—that massive, thick rubber tire designed for climbing rocks—rolled right up onto her legs and pelvis.

The car stopped. Not because of the brakes. It stopped because it was pinned on top of a two-year-old child.

The silence that followed lasted for a millisecond, but it felt like an eternity. Then came the scream. It didn’t come from Sarah. It came from Bella. A shriek of pure, unadulterated agony that shattered the afternoon peace. It was the sound of a bone snapping.

Sarah came running out of the house, dropping a gallon of milk. It exploded on the driveway, white liquid mixing with the dirt and the heat. She saw the car. She saw her baby underneath it. She collapsed. She didn’t faint; her legs just gave out from the sheer terror. She started crawling toward the car on her hands and knees, screaming, ""MY BABY! HELP! SOMEBODY HELP!""

I reached the scene first. My heart was hammering against my ribs like a trapped bird. I threw myself at the back of the SUV. I grabbed the bumper. ""Sarah, pull her out! I’m going to lift!""

I pulled. I strained. I gritted my teeth until I thought they would crack. I put every ounce of strength I had into lifting that vehicle.

It didn’t budge. Not a millimeter. It was a tank. A 5,000-pound mix of steel and iron, pressing down on fragile little bones.

Bella’s screams were turning into whimpers. That was worse. That meant she was fading. That meant the pressure was cutting off her blood flow.

""I can’t move it!"" I yelled, panic seizing my throat. ""It’s too heavy!""

Another neighbor, Bob, came running from two doors down. Bob is a big guy, plays weekend football, spends his time at the gym. He grabbed the other side. ""On three!"" he roared. ""One, two, three!""

We pulled. We heaved. Veins popped in my neck. My back screamed in protest. The heat was suffocating us.

The car rocked slightly, but the tire stayed planted on Bella. She was trapped. Crushed. And we were failing her. We were two grown men, the ""protectors"" of the neighborhood, and we were useless.

""Call 911!"" Sarah was sobbing, her hands covered in grease as she tried to dig her fingers under the tire, trying to claw the asphalt away to free her daughter. ""Please, God, please!""

I looked around, desperate. We needed a jack. We needed a tow truck. We needed a miracle, and we needed it five minutes ago.

What God Says About You
By Susan Pruitt Bolinger

People will always have opinions about you. Some will be favorable; others, not so much. But those opinions are birthed out of their experiences, not yours. People view you through the lens of their own character, wounds, and perceptions—and that’s exactly why their opinions should never define you. They will always be skewed.

God is the only One who knows you completely and fully—and He loves you more than anyone else ever could.

As I was reading Ephesians 1, something jumped right off the page. Out of twenty-three amazing verses, seventeen of them declare what God says about me. Right there in black and white. All in one chapter. I circled those words one by one because I needed that reminder.

God says…
I am faithful.
I am graceful.
I am peaceful.
I am blessed.
I am chosen.
I am holy.
I am without blame.
I am adopted.
I am accepted.
I am redeemed.
I am forgiven.
I am wise.
I am prudent.
I am saved.
I am sealed.
I am loved.

And God has given unto me the Spirit of wisdom, revelation, and knowledge.
Wow. How God loves His children.

God has never had a single bad thought about you! In fact, He has placed reminders throughout His Word to show you just how incredible He believes you are. Sit with these truths today. Relish them. Allow them to sink deep and penetrate your heart. 

Susan Bolinger - Bloom Ladies Ministry

Kedua kata ini (كافرون & كفار) sama-sama bahasa Arab. Keduanya juga terdapat dalam Alquran. Keduanya sama-sama bentuk jamak. Bentuk tunggalnya kàfir yang berasal dari kata "kafara" yang artinya penutup. Dalam bahasa Inggris disebut cover. Saya tidak tahu persis apakah berasal dari bahasa Inggris atau bahasa Inggris berasal dari bahasa Arab. Yang pasti bahasa-bahasa di dunia saling mempengaruhi. 
Kita juga mengenal "koper" yakni tempat menyimpan pakaian atau barang berharga dan selalu tertutup atau ditutup.

Doktor Harifuddin Cawidu (alm), dosen IAIN Alauddin Makasar -sekarang sudah UIN - pernah dijuluki doktor kafir. Disertasinya waktu kuliah di UIN Syahid Jakarta membahas tentang istilah kafir dalam Alquran. Menurutnya makna kafir dalam Alquran sekitar 40 an. 
Sebagian penganut agama non muslim ada yang alergi atau kurang setuju kalau disebut kaum kafir. Bahkan banyak juga umat Islam yang kurang setuju dengan sebutan kafir bagi non muslim. Padahal orang Islam disebut domba sesat oleh mereka. Tidak marah, tidak tersinggung. Karena itu istilah dalam kitab suci mereka. 
Begitu pula istilah kafir. Itu adalah istilah dalam Alquran. Bahkan nama salah satu surah dalam Alquran yakni surah al kafirun. Dalam surah tsb jelas ولا انتم عابدون ما اعبد. Dan kamu bukan penyembah apa yang aku sembah. Jelas bahwa kafir itu adalah yang menyembah selain Allah swt.  

Kata kuffàr (كفار) yang merupakan bentuk jamak dari kafir dalam Alquran maknanya bukan kafir yang menyembah selain Allah, melainkan para petani. Ini dapat dilihat pada surah al-Hadid ayat ke-20 :

Amiirkii Mu’miniinta Cali bin Abu Taalib Allaha raalli ka noqdee, markii uu ogaaday Talxa iyo Zubayr iyo Caa’isha Allaha raalli ka wada noqdee inay dhinaca Basra abbaareen oo aysan Kuufa aadin waa uu ku farxay maxaa yeelay Kuufa ayay taageerayaashiisu ku badnaayeen oo ciidan xoog leh uu ka filayey, oo wuxuu yiri: Reer Kuufa baan anigu jeclahay oo waxaa meeshaas jooga madaxdii Carabeed iyo dadkoodii magaca lahaa, markaasuu Cali Reer Kuufa dhambaal u sii diray oo iska sii hormariyey, wuxuuna u qornaa sidaan:

(KU BILAABID MAGACA ALLE NAXARIISTAAGA NAXARIISTA BADAN)

“Intaas kaddib, idinkaan idin doortay oo aan doonayaa inaan dhexdiinna dago, markii aan ogaaday gacalnimadiinna iyo jeclaanta aad Alle weyne iyo Rasuulkiisa scw u qabtaan, qofkii ii yimaada oo ii hiilliya xaqii buu raacay, waajibkii saarnaana waa uu gutay” …

Muxammad bin Abu Bakar Cali baa soo korsaday oo hooyadiis dumaalay, wuxuuna ka mid ahaa nimankii fallaagada ahaa oo xag jirka noqday oo Cismaan ku duulay, laakin Cali aabbe oo kale buu u arkayey oo si buuxda ayuu uu taageersanaa oo fallaagadu waxay isugu jireen dad kala duwan oo ujeeddooyin kala duwan leh oo xagjirnimada iyo nacaybka Cismaan ku midoobay oo dhammaantood uu si dadban dabada uga soo riixayey Yuhuudkii habaarnaa isagoo xer gaar ugu xiran lahaa inta kalana uugaan ku watay oo aan sirtiisa u sheegin, Cali waa uu ogaa Muxammad inuu ka mid ahaa fallaagadii Cismaan ku soo duushay laakin wuxuu u arkayey inuu wiilkiisii yahay oo daacad isaga u yahay sidaas daraaddeed inuu ka faa’idaysto buu doonayey oo Cali waxyaalo badan baa hoosta ka soo galay oo xalkoodu ka murugsanaa, halkaasna waxaa ka muuqata inuusan Cali dadkii Cismaan ku duulay oo dhan inay wada khaldan yihiin qabin, si uu yeelana ma uusan aqoon oo dadka hor boodaya oo taageersan barkood baa Cismaan ku duulay isla markaasna isagu u arkayey inuusan ka maarmi karin xilligaas….

“Alle weyne diinta islaamka ayuu nagu ciseeyey oo kor noogu qaaday, oo nagu walaaleeyey innagoo dulli ku noolayn oo tiro ahaan yarayn, oo nacayb iyo colaad dhexdeenna ahi ay nala hareen, intii Alle doonay bayna dadku sidaas ku socdeen oo islaamku diintooda ahaa, oo xaqu u dhexeeyey kitaabkuna hoggaankooda ahaa, ilaa ay ninkaas dileen duulkaas shayddaanku qalloociyey si uu ummaddaan isugu diro, hadde ummaddaanina waatii is khilaafta oo kala qaybsanta sidii ummadihii horaba u kala qaybsameen, Alle ayaan ka magan galaynnaa sharka waxa soo aaddane, misna waa ku soo celiyey mar kale oo wuxuu yiri: Wixii dhacayaa waa kii dhaca oo la fursan mayo, oo hooy ummaddaani waxay u kala qaybsami doontaa toddobaatan iyo saddex firqo, waxaana ugu shar badan firqo aniga i sheeganaysa oo aan dhaqankayga raacahayn, waadna aragteen oo soo gaarteen ee diintiinna ku dhaga oo hanuunkii nabigiinna scw raaca iyo dhaqankiisii wixii shaki idinka galana Quraanka Alle u bandhiga, oo wuxuu Quraanku sugo ku dhega, wixii uu diidana iska celiya, oo raalli ku ahaada inuu Alle weyne Abbaan idiin ahaado Islaamkuna diin idiin ahaado Muxammadna nabi idiin ahaado Quraankuna xukun iyo hoggaan idiin ahaado”

Cali Allaha raalli ka noqdee oo bad ku ahaa cilmiga diinta ummadda waa la taliyey oo u warramay waxyaalaha dhaxalka ahna waxaa ka mid ahaa inay Cismaan dileen dad habaaran oo fidno bilaabay, sidoo kale wuxuu sheegay firqooyinka ummaddu u kala baxayso inay ugu shar badnaan doonto qolo magaciisa iyo taageeradiisa sheeganaysa dhaqankiisa iyo diintana ka fog, waa shiicada Cali sanamka ka dhigta oo xadkiisa dhaafisa oo saxaabadii Rasuulka oo dhan qofaf kooban ma ahee gaaleyey kuwaas oo ah waliba Shiicada Raafidada loo yaqaan oo shiicada u shar badan, kuwaas oo qaba in Alle iyo Rasuulkiisu amreen in Cali iyo firkiisuu dhaxalka talinta ummadda leeyihiin ciddii kale oo qabatayna ay ka xoogeen oo amarkii Alle iyo Rasuulka jabiyeen oo sidaas gaalo ku noqdeen, waa shayaaddiin caqiidadii Yuhuudka xanbaaray….

2- Labadooduba way lumeen.

Inta u dhaxaysa erayada:

{Oo way tuureen} oo {Sidaa ayay u tuureen}

Qasriga uu Yuusuf ku noolaa:

Ninkii ayaa ahaa kii codsaday in Yuusuf lagu koriyo daryeelkiisa.

Kii Masar ka soo iibsadayna wuxuu xaaskiisa ku yidhi, "Degenaanshihiisa ka dhig mid raaxo leh; laga yaabee inuu na anfaco, ama aan korsanno wiil ahaan."

7- Xaaskii milkiilaha qasriga uu Muuse ku noolaa waxay ahayd ilo ammaan ah.

Xaaskii milkiilaha qasriga uu Yuusuf ku noolaa waxay ahayd ilo dhibaato iyo walaac ah.

8- Qur'aanku wuxuu ka hadlayaa labada nin ee qaangaarnimada gaaray laba siyaabood oo isku mid ah:

Jidka (Yuusuf), nabadgalyo korkiisa ha ahaatee:

"Markuu qaangaarayna, waxaan siinay xigmad iyo aqoon. Sidaasaana ku abaalmarinnaa kuwa wanaagga fala."

Jidka (Nabi Muuse), nabadgalyo korkiisa ha ahaatee:

"Markuu qaangaaray oo uu gaaray xooggiisii ​​oo dhan, waxaan siinay xigmad iyo aqoon. Sidaasaana ku abaalmarinnaa kuwa wanaagga fala."

9- Qur'aanku wuxuu ka sheekaynayaa murugadii hooyadiis Muuse:

"Qalbiga hooyadiis Muuse wuu madhnaa."

Sheekada aabaha Yuusuf ayaa sidoo kale la sheegay. Marka laga hadlayo sharraxaadda Qur'aanka ee murugadiisa:

"Alla, murugadayda Yuusuf! Indhihiisuna waxay u caddaatay murugo."

10- Walaalihii Yuusuf ayaa ahaa kuwii tuuray oo dhaawacay.

Walaashii Muuse ayaa ahayd tii raadinaysay oo caawisay.

11- Markii Muuse la raadinayay, waxay ahayd hooyadii Muuse oo codsatay raadinta waxayna u dirtay walaashiis:

"Waxayna ku tidhi walaashiis, 'Raac isaga.'"

Markii Yuusuf la raadinayay, wuxuu ahaa aabbihii Yuusuf oo codsaday raadinta wuxuuna diray walaalihiis Yuusuf:

"Wiilashayow, taga oo raadiya Yuusuf."

12- Bilowgii gargaarka hooyadii Muuse iyadoo la kulmay wiilkeeda:

Bilowgii gargaarka Aabbihii Yuusuf, markuu la kulmay wiilkiisa:

13- Rabbiga Caalamku wuxuu u muujiyay hooyadiis Muuse inuu wiilkeeda u celin doono:

"Runtii, waan kuu soo celin doonnaa oo waxaan ka dhigi doonnaa mid ka mid ah rasuullada."

Rabbi Caalamku wuxuu u muujiyay aabihiis Yuusuf inuu wiilkiisa u celin doono:

"Waxaana ka ogahay Ilaah wax aadan aqoon."

#Puntland: Ganacsade xukun cadaalad-darro ah ay ku riday maxkamadaha Puntland iyo musuq lagu eedeeyay hay’adaha caddaaladda Puntland.

Ganacsade lagu magacaabo Cabdilaahi Xasan Siciid, oo shirkad gadiid ku lahaa magaalada Gaalkacyo, ayaa muddo dheer wajahaya wax ay qoyskiisu ku tilmaameen xadgudub sharci, xukun cadaalad daro ku dhisan iyo gorgortan lacageed oo lagu furtay.

Cabdilaahi Xasan Siciid, sida ay qoysku sheegeen, waxa uu raray alaab ganacsi oo isugu jirtay moobeelo iyo chargers, kuwaas oo laga soo diray magaalada Muqdisho, kuna sii jeeday Boosaaso. Alaabtaas, sida xogta lagu helay, dawladda ayaa baaritaan ku samaysay, cashuur ka qaaday, kadibna si rasmi ah loogu soo dhiibay xafiiska ay khusayso, isaga oo buuxiyey dhammaan waajibaadkiisii ganacsi.

Inkasta oo alaabtaasi ay ahayd mid dadkii lahaa iyo kuwii soo dirayba la yaqaan, haddana Cabdilaahi ayaa la xiray 25-kii Juun 2024 magaalada Gaalkacyo, waxaana 1-dii Luulyo 2024 loo wareejiyey Garoowe. halkaas oo uu ku xirnaa ku dhowaad 10 bilood maxkamad la’aan, arrin qoyska iyo dad u dhuun-daloola xuquuqda aadanaha ku tilmaameen afduub sharci-darro ah.

Qoyska Cabdilaahi waxay sheegeen in madaxa Baarista Dambiyada Gobolka Nugaal, Mahad Cabdi Faloow uu cadaadis dhaqaale saaray qoyska, isaga oo ka dalbaday lacag si kiiska maxkamad loo horgeeyo, inkasta oo, sida ay sheegayaan, aysan jirin dambi rasmi ah oo lagu hayay eedaysanaha, hadana horkeenista ayuu lacag uga qaatay.

Waxaa xusid mudan in 9-kii Abriil 2025, Cabdilaahi markii la horgeeyay maxkamad, taas oo timid kadib 10 bilood oo xarig sharci-darro ah, arrin si cad uga hor imaanaysa dastuurka iyo xeerarka dalka.

Intii uu socday kiiska, mar kasta oo maxkamad la ballamiyo, waxaa la sheegay in Xeer Ilaaliyuhu uu gooyo, iyadoo qoyska ay ku eedeeyeen isla Mahad Cabdi Faloow inuu si toos ah ugu lug lahaa go’aannadaas si lacago dheeri ah uu u hello markale.

Dhageysigii ugu dambeeyay, maxkamaddu waxay ku xukuntay Cabdilaahi laba sano oo xarig ah kaas oo lagu sheegay ganaax, iyada oo lagu eedeeyay inuu alaab uusan hubsan uusii dhiibay. Si kastaba ha ahaatee, qoyska waxay sheegeen in alaabtii moobeelada ahayd ee CID-du qabatay ilaa maanta aan la hayn wax xog ah oo ku saabsan halka ay ku dambeysay.

Waxaa kale oo qoyska ay tilmaameen in lacag gaaraysa ku dhowaad $6,000 laga qaaday intii uu socday kiiska, halka maxkamaddu ay qaadatay $1,600 si loogu sii daayo eedaysanaha.

Qoyska Cabdilaahi Xasan Siciid, oo kasoo jeeda beesha Nuurkiqabe (Majeerteen), ayaa sheegay inaysan wax xil ah ku lahayn dawladda Puntland, isla markaana aysan haysan cid awood leh oo u doodda, taas oo ay rumeysan yihiin inay sabab u noqotay dulmiga ay wajahayaan, sidoo kale ay tuhunsan yihiin i magacii dawladnimada Puntland lagu dulmiyay.

Cabdilaahi Garwayen waa aabare qoys balaaran leh oo masruuf iyo biil ay ka sugayaan caruur tirabadan, sidoo kale waxa uu ka tirsanaa kooxda Ikhlaas ( Takfiir loo yaqaan) kuwaas oo aan ka mid ahayn kooxaha khilaafaadka dalka aan ku luglahayn.

Ugu dambeyn, sida ay qoyska Cabdilaahi Xasan Siciid iyo dad kale oo bulsho ku dhex jira sheegeen, Mahad Cabdi Faloow waxa uu isku darsaday labo xil oo sharci ahaan kala madax-bannaan denbi-baare iyo xeer ilaaliye —arrin si weyn su’aal uga keenaysa dhexdhexaadnimada iyo hufnaanta nidaamka caddaaladda. 

Qoyska iyo ilo kale oo warbixino nala wadaagay ayaa ku adkaysanaya in Mahad uu yahay nin horey ugu lug lahaa kiisas caan ah, kuwaas oo ay ku doodayaan in dulmi iyo ku tumasho xuquuqeed uu ugu geystay dad bulshada sumcad ku lahaa.

Cabashooyinka la xiriira hab-dhaqanka Mahad Cabdi Faloow, sida ay ilo-wareedyo bulsho sheegeen, ma aha kuwo hal mar ah, balse waa eedeymo soo noqnoqday oo mar kasta gaara weriyeyaasha, qareennada iyo dadka u dhuun-daloola xuquuqda aadanaha. Taasi waxay abuureysaa sawir halis ah oo muujinaya kalsooni darro sii kordhaysa oo ku wajahan hay’adaha caddaaladda, gaar ahaan marka qof keliya uu yeesho awood uu ku baaro, ku eedeeyo, kuna gorgortamo isla kiiska.

Sidaa darteed, warbixintan oo ku saleysan xog qoyska iyo cabashooyin bulsho, waxay si cad u muujinaysaa baahida loo qabo in dawladda Puntland ay si degdeg ah uga falceliso eedeymahan culus, isla markaana ay qaaddo tallaabooyin muuqda oo lagu joojinayo ku takri-falka shaarka dawladda ee lagu dulminayo muwaadiniinta. 

Waxaa laga sugayaa hay’adaha ay khusayso in la sameeyo baaritaan madax-bannaan, laguna kala saaro awoodaha sharci, si loo xaqiijiyo in caddaaladdu noqoto mid u adeegta shacabka, kana madaxbannaan dano shaqsi iyo gorgortan lacageed.

1. Qabiil iyo nidaamka 4.5 (Identity Politics)🇸🇴 
• Nidaamka 4.5 waa tusaale cad oo siyaasadda aqoonsiga ah.
• Qabiillada waaweyn iyo kuwa laga tirada badan yahay waxaa loo kala qoondeeyey kuraas si “aqoonsi” loo siiyo.
• Dhinaca wanaagsan: 
• Wuxuu keenay ka-qaybgal ballaaran kadib burburkii dawladda.
• Dhinaca taban: 
• Wuxuu adkeeyey kala-qaybsanaanta qabiilka halkii uu ka dhisi lahaa muwaadinnimo wadaag ah.
2. Beelaha laga tirada badan yahay (Recognition)
• Beelaha sida Banaadiri, Bantu/Jareer, Yibir, Tumaal, Gaboye.
• Dalabkoodu waa: 
• In la aqoonsado taariikhdooda, takooriddii hore, iyo xuquuqdooda.
• Tusaale: 
• Ku-darista kuraas gaar ah ama cod gaar ah shirarka qaran → ictiraaf.
3. Federaalka iyo Aqoonsiga Gobollada
• Maamul-goboleedyadu (Puntland, Jubbaland, Koonfur Galbeed, iwm).
• Qabiilo iyo deegaanno waxay ku doodayaan: 
• “Annagu waxaan leenahay aqoonsi gaar ah iyo xuquuq maamul.”
• Tani waa isku-dar: 
• Aqoonsi deegaan + siyaasad aqoonsi.
4. Luqadda iyo Dhaqanka (Cultural Recognition)
• Doodaha ku saabsan: 
• Adeegsiga lahjadaha Maay iyo Maxaa-tiri ee waxbarashada iyo warbaahinta.
• Dalabka: 
• In luqadahaas la aqoonsado, loona isticmaalo adeegyada dadweynaha.
• Tani waa ictiraaf dhaqan.
5. Haweenka iyo qoondada 30% (Gender Identity Politics)
• Ololaha qoondada 30% haweenka ee baarlamaanka.
• Haweenku waxay ku doodayaan: 
• In aqoonsigooda jinsiyadeed la tixgeliyo.
• Tani waa: 
• Siyaasad aqoonsi oo ku wajahan sinnaanta.
6. Dhalinyarada iyo Ka-qaybgalka Siyaasadda
• Inkastoo ay yihiin tirada ugu badan bulshada, haddana matalaaddoodu way yar tahay.
• Dhalinyaradu waxay dalbanayaan: 
• In la aqoonsado doorkooda horumarineed.
• Tani waa ictiraaf jiil (generational recognition).
7. Qaxoontiga iyo Barakacayaasha Gudaha (IDPs)
• Barakacayaasha gudaha waxay dalbanayaan: 
• Adeegyo, dhul, iyo xuquuq muwaadinimo.
• Aqoonsigooda “dad nugul” waa ictiraaf bulsho.

Dowladda ay rabaan ama inta badan la sawirto, waa dowlad “diimaysan”, taas oo saldhiggeedu yahay Kitaabka iyo Sunnada, halka marjaca ugu dambeeya ee go’aan kasta lagu laabto uu noqdo diinta Islaamka. Aragtidan ayaa si weyn uga dhex muuqata hadalka bulshada, doodaha siyaasadda, iyo himilooyinka la xiriira mustaqbalka dalka.

Hase yeeshee, marka la eego nidaamka dowladnimo ee dunida maanta ka jira, inta badan dowladuhu waa dowlado cilmaani ah, ama ugu yaraan, dowlado kala saaray diinta iyo maamulka dawladeed. Dowladahan waxay ku dhisan yihiin qodobbo cad, dhul la aqoonsan yahay, xuduud, sharciyo qoran, muwaadinimo (citizenship), iyo hay’ado maamula danaha qaranka. Muwaadinku xuquuq buu leeyahay, waajibaad buu leeyahay, diinta uu haystana kuma xirna helidda xuquuqdaas.

Halkaas ayay mushkiladda ugu weyn ee Soomaalida ka bilaabataa, Dunida maanta kama jirto dowlad si rasmi ah ugu dhisan “wax Islaam ah” oo ka baxsan qaab dowladnimo caalami ah. Dowlad walba, xitaa kuwa Muslimiintu waxay ku shaqeeyaan nidaam qaran: dano qaran, sharciyo qaran, xuduud qaran, iyo xiriir dibadeed oo ku salaysan maslaxad (interest),  ee kuma dhisna caqiido kali ah.

Dowladuhu waxay la macaamilaan cid kasta oo ay dano wadaagaan: dhaqaale, amni, ganacsi, khayraad ama siyaasadda gobolka, iyadoon loo eegin diinta ay haystaan. Muwaadinnimada ayaa ah tiirka ee a aha diinta. Sidaas darteed, dowladdu si siman ayay ula dhaqantaa qof kasta oo dhalasheeda haysta, diin kasta ha haystee.

Marka si dhab ah loo eego aragtida caalamiga ah, cadownimada dowladuhu kama timaaddo kala duwanaansho diimeed, dhaqan ama bulsho. Cadownimadu waxay ka dhalataa:
 • Loollan dhuleed
 • Khilaaf xuduudeed
 • Tartanka khayraadka
 • Isbahaysiyo iyo dano iska hor imanaya

Aragtida dowladnimada ee diimaysan waa mid aan ku dhisnayn wax la dhaho dan ee ku dhisan diin, muwaadin walba oo ashaadanaya waxay siinaysaa xaq dhamaystiran, waxay xeerinaysaa shuruuda u degsan kitaabkeeda, ciddii kitaabku fogeeyay waa in la fogeeyo, cidduu soo dhaweeyay waa in la dhawaysto, waa in diiwaankeedu ku jiraan umad loo yaqaan gaalo oo la iska dheereeyo, adigu isku soo wada duubo sharci iyo qaanuun hoostagaya xeerarka islaamiga, taasina dunida maanta kama aha suuragal, iskaashiga, taageeridda, is garab istaaga, xulufaysiga iyo gaashaanbuursiguba wuxuu ku dhisan yahay dano adduunyo iyo duruufo amni, dhaqaale, siyaasadeed iyo xeelado is garabsi. Hadaba halkee bay somalidu kasoo galaysaa dowladnimada noocaas ah marka ay umadii kale gaalnimo uga soo urto oo ay qori isaga qabtaan, waa sidaas bay somalidu ku tahay umad sabool ah, burbursan oo dhaqaale ahaan liita, goorma ayay helaysaa awood ay ku meel mariso aragtideeda dowladnimo?

Somaliland waa dal si iskiis ah isu maamulaayey tan iyo 1991, leh dawlad, dastuur, doorashooyin, nabad, iyo xuduud la ilaaliyo. Ka indho-tiridda xaqiiqadan ma beddelayso jiritaankeeda, balse waxay sii fogaynaysaa wada-hadal macno leh.

2. Inay joojiyaan hadalka nacaybka iyo been-abuurka
Af-lagaaddada, caayda, iyo warbaahinta lagu faafinayo naceybku ma aha siyaasad, mana aha waddaniyad. Waa burbur bulsho iyo sharaf-darro ku dhacaysa qofka hadlaya ka hor inta aanu cid kale gaadhin.

3. Inay bartaan taariikhda si caddaalad ah
Midowgii 1960 wuxuu ku dhisnaa rajo, balse wuxuu ku dhammaaday tacaddi, xasuuq, iyo dulmi la hubo. Kala-go’a Somaliland ma ahayn damac, ee wuxuu ahaa badbaado iyo badbaadin dad iyo dal.

4. Inay ixtiraamaan rabitaanka shacabka Somaliland
Rabitaanka dad waa saldhigga sharciyadda caalamiga ah. Shacabka Somaliland afti ayay ku doorteen masiirkooda. Qof aan rabitaankaas ixtiraamayn, dimuqraadiyad hadal kama geli karo.

5. Inay doortaan wada-hadal halkii ay ka dooran lahaayeen hanjabaad
Haddii wax la wada leeyahay la sheeganayo, wada-hadal ayaa loo maraa, ee ma aha qaylo, warbaahin, iyo hanjabaad madhan.

6. Inay diiradda saaraan dhibaatooyinkooda gaarka ah
Soomaaliya waxay haysataa caqabado waaweyn: amni, midnimo, horumar, iyo dowlad-dhis. Ka mashquulidda Somaliland ma xallinayso midna.

Somaliland ma dalbanayso oggolaansho jiritaankeeda, balse waxay mudan tahay ixtiraam. Qof kasta oo Soomaali ah oo doonaya mustaqbal nabdoon oo Geeska Afrika ah, waa inuu aqbalaa kala-duwanaanta, xaqiiqda, iyo rabitaanka shucuubta.

Alle ha u naxariistee, Shiikh Cumar Faaruuq (RC) ayaa mar hadal xikmad iyo aragti dheer xambaarsan ku yiri:
“Soomaalida ilaali, kala ilaali, iskana ilaali. Ummaddan Soomaaliyeed waa ummad si walba u dayacan; iskuma roona ee kala ilaali.”
Hadalkan qiimaha badan ayuu si gaar ah ugu dardaarmay Madaxweynihii Jamhuuriyadda Jabuuti, Mudane Ismaaciil Cumar Geelle.
Hadalkaas ma ahayn mid caadi ah, mana ahayn hadal ku eg waqti gaar ah; wuxuu ahaa digniin taariikhi ah, talo ka dhalatay waaya-aragnimo, aqoon iyo faham qoto dheer oo ku saabsan xaaladda ummadda Soomaaliyeed. Maanta, sanado badan kadib, hadalkaas wali waa mid nool, wali waa mid quseeya, wali waa mid u baahan in si dhab ah loo fahmo.
Soomaalidu waa ummad leh taariikh dheer, diin mideysa, dhaqan wadaag ah iyo dhiig isku xiran, balse nasiib darro waxa ay noqotay ummad si sahlan loo kala kicin karo, loo kala faa’iideysan karo, loona adeegsado dano shisheeye iyo kuwo shaqsiyeed. Waxaa nagu batay is eedeyn, is nacayb, qabyaalad, kala shaki iyo dano gaar ah oo laga hormariyo masiirka guud ee ummadda.
Shiikh Cumar Faaruuq markuu yiri “kala ilaali”, ma uusan wadin in la kala fogaado, balse wuxuu ula jeeday in laga digtoonaado dhaawaca ka iman kara marka ummaddu isugu tagto si aan nidaam, iimaan iyo is tixgelin ku jirin. “Iskana ilaali” wuxuu ahaa digniin ku socota hoggaamiyeyaasha, culimada iyo dadka saamaynta leh, si aysan u noqon kuwo si fudud loogu adeegto ama loogu adeegsado dhibaateynta dadkooda.
Maanta, xaaladda Soomaalida meelkasta oo ay joogaan—Gudaha dalka, Geeska Afrika iyo daafaha dunida—waxay marqaati u tahay runnimada hadalkaas. Kala aragti la’aan, kala danbayn la’aan iyo hoggaan xumo ayaa weli caqabad ku ah horumarka, midnimada iyo karaamada ummadda Soomaaliyeed.
Haddaba, waa waajib in aan dib ugu noqono xikmadda culimadeenna, talada waayeelkeenna, iyo casharrada taariikhdeena. Waa in aan fahamnaa in cadowga ugu weyn ee Soomaalida uusan mar walba ahayn mid dibadda ka yimaada, balse inta badan uu yahay kan ka dhex shaqeeya, kana faa’iideysta kala qaybsanaanteenna.
Hadalka Shiikh Cumar Faaruuq wuxuu ahaa baaq wacyi, baaq badbaado, iyo baaq mas’uuliyad. Haddii aan si dhab ah u qaadan lahayn, maanta sawirka Soomaalida meel kale ayuu ahaan lahaa.
Alle ha u naxariisto Shiikha, hana na siiyo garasho aan ku fahanno hadalkiisa, iyo awood aan ku saxno jidka aan ku soconno.

Waxaan arkay dadkii waqtigeenna oo ka dhigtay mabda’ooda nololeed is-beddel joogto ah iyo midab-rogasho; halka ku adkaysiga qiyamka loo arko “nijaas fikir.” Qofkii Islaamiga ahaa ee shalay u dagaallami jiray fikrad iyo ideolojiyad, kana tarbiyayn jiray dadka, maanta wuxuu si aan xishood lahayn ugu yeedhayaa qabyaalad, xataa carruurtiisana ku barbaariyaa jacaylkeeda iyo u hiilinteeda—xitaa haddii ay mabaadi’da ka hor imanayso.

Is-beddelku dad qaar kuma noqdo wax lala yaabo, balse yaabka ugu weyn wuxuu yimaadaa marka la arko waayeel adkaystay oo la is weydiiyo: sidee bay u suurtagashay in ay adkaystaan? Maanta, wax la moodo caqli iyo xeelad ayaa noqotay in la macaansado arrimaha diinta iyo fikirka, halka shalay ay ahayd munaafaqnimo. Waa is-khilaafaad waqti iyo is-rogrogasho duruufo. Waxaan hore u aragnay dad ku dagaallami jiray in ay nagu wacyigeliyaan xaaraantinimada u galidda albaabada siyaasiyiinta; maanta se waxaan arkay iyaga oo si xad-dhaaf ah ugu dhowaada, kuna dooda in ka fogaanshahoodu yahay fitno. Ilaahayna abuurkiisa wuu kala leeyahay arrimo.

Waxaan is weydiiyey sababta; waxaanan ogaaday in badankood ay u gutaan cibaadada cibaadada lafteeda awgeed—ee aan ka badan.

3. Dadku way jecel yihiin wacdinta; waxay doortaan dacwiyeyaasha codkoodu xooggan yahay, kuwa dareenka kiciyana u soo xaadiraan meel walba. Hase yeeshee, waxa nolosha ka haraya hadalkooda waa yar. Waxaan is iri: maxaa sababa? Waxaan ogaaday in dadku u jecel yihiin hadalka dacwiyeyaasha sida ay u jecel yihiin heesaha fannaaniinta iyo suugaanta gabyaa—way u harraad yihiin diinta, balse ma fahansana in diintu tahay mashruuc nololeed, ee aan ahayn wacdi kaliya. Sidaas darteed, waxaan mar kale is weydiiyey—anigoo murugo weyn dareemaya—yaa mas’uul ka ah hoos-u-dhacan fikirka ummadda? Waxaan qirtay in dhibku ku jiro hadal dacwiyayaal ka madhan nuxur fikir, oo ku mashquulsan muuqaal.

4. Waxaan arkay Muslimiin Galbeedka ku nool oo ka baqaya milanka aqoonsiga, kana walwala mustaqbalka carruurtooda; hase yeeshee aan marna raadin xal iyo mashruuc guud oo jiilasha lagu badbaadiyo. Waxaan is weydiiyey: maxay xal u raadin waayeen halkii ay ka hadli lahaayeen cabsi joogto ah? Khibraddayda Canada iyo Maraykan waxay muujisay in kooxaha Muslimiinta ahi ka liitaan aqoonta culuumta bulsho, kana fogaadeen mashruuc ilbaxnimo oo ummadda ka badbaadin kara milanka iyo luminta aqoonsiga—maadaama ay Galbeedka yimaadeen iyagoo aan garanayn sababta ay u joogaan, iyo inay doonayaan inay noqdaan Muslimiin Galbeedka ku nool mise inay ku noolaadaan qurbajoog joogto ah.

Cabsidu xal ma aha; xalku waa ka gudbidda cabsida iyo ka xoroobidda ku fikirka joogtada ah ee ku noqoshada Bariga—waayo duruufuhu taas ma taageerayaan, taariikhduna kama warramin hirar dadnimo oo dib u laabta. Waxaan hubnaa in dunidu dhan Ilaahay u wada tirsan tahay, Muslimkuna yahay mid aragti caalami ah leh; la tacaalidda caqabaduhuna waa lama huraan Bariga iyo Galbeedka, inkastoo ay kala duwanaan karto nooca caqabadaha.

Kadib feker iyo baaritaan, waxaan ogaaday in ka-mid-noqoshadu tahay dabeecad, diin, ilbaxnimo, iyo baahi. Qabiil iyo qarannimo waa dabeecad, balse bani’aadamnimo ahaan kuma filna. Waayeelka fahmay arrintan awgeed ayaan maanta ku aragnaa kuwo doorbidaya ka-mid-noqoshada fikirka halkii ay ka ahaan lahayd qabyaalad noqotay caqabad culus oo hor istaagta horumarinta Afrika iyo dunida Carabta.

Soomaaliya, Xukunka iyo Xisaabtan La’aanta: Maxkamad Ma Hagagi Doontaa?

Su’aasha ah in hoggaamiyeyaasha dhibaatada u gaysta Soomaaliya mar uun maxkamad la soo taagi doono waa su’aal weli furan, balse xaqiiqdu waa mid qadhaadh: xisaabtan dhab ah weli ma jiro. Tan iyo burburkii dowladdii dhexe, dalka waxa marar badan xukumay dad magacyo kala duwan wata, balse hal sifo wadaaga—mas’uuliyad la’aan iyo ciqaab ka badbaadis.

Dowladihii ka dambeeyay burburka, gaar ahaan kuwii ku yimid xaalad kala guur ah, waxa ay galeen khaladaad waaweyn: ku tuman xuquuqda muwaadiniinta, hurinta colaad qabiil, musuq, iyo ku ciyaaridda masiirka qaranka. Natiijadu waxay noqotay qax, dhimasho, faqri iyo kala daadasho bulsho. Haddana, halkii laga filayay in la helo hannaan lagu xisaabtamo, waxa la arkayaa dadkii dhibaatadaas sababay oo maanta dalka dib ugu soo laabanaya—iyagoo xukun doon ah.

Tani ma aha arrin iska dhacday; waa dhaqan siyaasadeed oo qaldan. Soomaaliya waxa ka jira caado ah in hoggaamiye fashilmay ama dambi galay uusan wajahin caddaalad, balse uu helo cafis aan sharci ahayn, ama uu iska beddelo magac iyo isbahaysi si uu mar kale u helo awood. Taasi waxay diraysaa farriin halis ah: “Dembi samee, mar uun waad soo laabanaysaa.”

Maxkamad la’aan, xasuus la’aan, iyo qirasho la’aan—saddexdan ayaa ah sunta ugu weyn ee hor istaagta bogsashada qaranka. Dal walba oo dagaal sokeeye ka soo kabanaya waxa uu maraa marxalado ay ka mid yihiin run-sheegid, caddaalad, iyo dib-u-heshiisiin dhab ah. Soomaaliya se inta badan waxa la doortaa waddada gaaban: “Ha la iska illoobo wixii dhacay.” Laakiin wixii la illoobo way soo noqdaan—xaalad ka daran tii hore.

Waxaa ka sii daran in dadkii dhibaatada geystay ay maanta isu sawiraan badbaadiyeyaal, iyagoo adeegsanaya warbaahin, qabiil, ama dano shisheeye. Qaar waxay ku doodaan “waayo-aragnimo,” balse su’aasha runta ahi waa: waayo-aragnimo noocee ah? Mid dhisaysa mise mid burburisay? Haddii waayo-aragnimadu ahayd burbur, qax, iyo kala-qaybin, maxay mar kale u mudan yihiin kalsooni?

Caddaaladdu ma aha aargoosi; waa xaqiiqo la wajahayo. Maxkamad la soo taago hoggaamiye dembi galay micnaheedu ma aha in dalka la kala diro, balse waa in la yiraahdo: “Qof walba sharciga waa la mid.” Haddii aan la helin xisaabtan, jiil walba wuxuu ku korayaa faham ah in awooddu ka sarrayso sharciga—taas oo dhalinaysa hoggaamiyeyaal ka sii liita kuwii ka horreeyay.

Ugu dambayn, haddii Soomaaliya rabto mustaqbal ka duwan taariikhdeeda madow, waa in ay ka baxdaa wareegga xukun-doonka ee aan xisaabta lahayn. Waa in la dhisaa hay’ado caddaaladeed oo madax-bannaan, la diiwaangeliyo dambiyada waaweyn, lana joojiyo siyaasadda “waji cusub, qalad hore.” Intaas la’aanteed, dadkii dhibaatada ugu badan gaystay way soo noqonayaan—mar kasta—iyagoo rajaynaya in xusuusta ummaddu gaaban tahay.

Xaqiiqdu waa tan: Dal aan xisaabtamin ma horumaro; dal aan xasuusan dambigiisana wuu ku celceliyaa. Soomaaliya door bay leedahay—caddaalad iyo run, ama wareeg aan dhammaad lahayn.

Khatarta Muuqaalada AI iyo Sumcad-Dilista Madaxda & Bulshada

⸻

Maanta dunidu waxay gashay xilli cusub oo teknoolajiyad ah, gaar ahaan Artificial Intelligence (AI). Teknoolajiyaddan waxay leedahay faa’iidooyin badan, balse sidoo kale waxay keentay dhibaatooyin halis ah, gaar ahaan marka loo adeegsado sameynta muuqaalo been abuur ah (Deepfake).

Muuqaalada AI-ga lagu sameeyo waxaa lagu abuuri karaa cod, wajiyo, iyo hadallo u eg qof dhab ah, iyadoo qofkaasi uusan waligiis samayn. Taasi waxay abuurtay khatar weyn oo sumcad-dil, marin-habaabin, iyo qalqal bulsho.

Mid ka mid ah dhibaatada ugu weyn waa in madax, masuuliyiin, culimo, ganacsato, iyo dad caadi ah lagu sameeyo muuqaalo anshax-xumo ah ama hadallo been ah, kadibna lagu faafiyo baraha bulshada. Dad badan ayaa rumaysta muuqaalka, iyagoo aan hubin xaqiiqadiisa.

Tani waxay keentaa:
 • In la burburiyo sumcadda qof muddo daqiiqado ah
 • In la abuuro nacayb, colaad iyo qalqal amni
 • In la dhaawaco kalsoonida shacabka ee hoggaanka
 • In dad aan waxba galabsan lagu eedeeyo falal aysan samayn

Madaxda lagu hayo dhibaatooyinkan waxay la kulmaan cadaadis maskaxeed, hanjabaado, iyo mararka qaar xitaa khatar nololeed. Qaar badan ayaa lagu qasbaa inay ka aamusan arrinta, maadaama runta ay ka gaabin karto been si degdeg ah u faafaysa.

Sidoo kale, dhibaatadu kuma koobna madaxda oo kaliya. Haween, dhalinyaro, iyo ganacsato ayaa lagu sameeyaa muuqaalo anshax-xumo ah si loogu handado, lacag looga qaato, ama sumcad looga dilo. Tani waa xadgudub xuquuqeed iyo dambi.

Bulshadeenna Soomaaliyeed, oo horey u la daalaa dhacaysay warar been ah iyo marin-habaabin, AI-ga si khaldan loo adeegsado wuxuu sii kordhinayaa jahawareerka. Dad badan ma kala saari karaan run iyo been, gaar ahaan marka muuqaalka uu u egyahay mid dhab ah.

Haddaba maxaa xal ah?

Marka koowaad, wacyigelin bulsho ayaa loo baahan yahay. Dadka waa in la baraa inaysan rumaysan muuqaal kasta oo ay arkaan, isla markaana ay hubiyaan xogta.

Marka labaad, sharciyo adag ayaa loo baahan yahay si loo xakameeyo isticmaalka khaldan ee AI, loona ciqaabo cid kasta oo u adeegsata sumcad-dil iyo dhibaato bulsho.

Marka saddexaad, madaxda, hay’adaha dowliga ah, iyo warbaahinta waa inay yeeshaan hab degdeg ah oo been-abuurka lagu beeniyo, si aan beentu u noqon mid ka horreysa runta.

Ugu dambeyn, AI waa qalab awood badan. Waxay noqon kartaa fursad horumar ama hub burburin—wax walba waxay ku xiran yihiin sida aan u isticmaalno.

Haddii aan si wadajir ah u feejignaanno, u baraarugno, una istaagno xaqa, waxaan ka hortagi karnaa dhibaatada muuqaallada AI ee sumcad-dilka ah.

Mahadsanidiin.

MEERAHA COLAADDA AWDAL GASHEY: DAGAAL AAN DHAMMAAD LAHAYN, SHACABKUNA AYSAN KA FAA’IIDI DOONIN. 
Waxaan rabaa inaan la wadaago bulshada Soomaaliyeed, gaar ahaan dadka ku nool gobollada Awdal, Salal, iyo guud ahaan Soomaalida kale, aragti ku saabsan colaadaha  bilaabmey oo soo noqnoqdoona oo aan weligood miro dhali doonin.
Dagaalkan waa mid aan lahayn dhammaad cad, waana colaad ila meereyso ah oo mar walba ku soo laaban doonta isla meeshii ay ka bilaabantay. Waa dagaal u dhexeeya walaalo isku abtirsiin ah, halka qabiil walba uu isu arko mid is-difaacaya, balse xaqiiqadu tahay in labaduba ay ku dambaynayaan khasaare joogto ah, dhiig-bax iyo burbur bulsho. Ma jiro dhul la kala qabsandoono, mana jiridoonto cid sharaf ku helaysa, mana jiro mustaqbal ka soo baxaysa colaaddan, marka laga reebo naceyb, dhiigdaata, xanuun, barakac iyo kala shaki sii kordhidoona.
Cidda kaliya ee mar walba ka faa’iideysanidoonta waa kuwa ka shaqeynaya daaha gadaashiisa. Waa dillaaliin colaadeed oo ku kala sugan Somaliland, Soomaaliya, Jabuuti, Kililka Shanaad iyo meelo kale, kuwaas oo aan lahayn waddaniyad, damiir iyo naxariis toona. Waxay awoodaan inay nabad dhex dhigaan walaalaha is haya, waxay garanayaan sida colaadda loo joojin karo, balse si ula kac ah ayey usameeyaan, sababtoo ah nabaddu waxay ka dhigan tahay dhammaadka danahooda, magacooda iyo macaashka ay ka helayaan dhiigga shacabka.
Mar kasta oo ay muuqato in dadku daaleen, ama colaadda ay qaboobayso, ama rajo nabadeed ay soo baxeyso, isla dillaaliintaas ayaa dib u hurinaya dabka. Waxay adeegsadaan cabsi, qabyaalad, warar been ah iyo kicin shucuur si ay u sii wadaan ilameeraysada iyo colaadda. Dadka Soomaaliyeed ee is-dilaya ma aha kuwo ka faa’iidaya dagaalkan, balse waa dad dhibanayaal ah oo loo adeegsanayo fulinta ajandayaal shisheeye iyo dano gaar ah oo cid gaar ahi leedahay.
Haddii aanan si miyir leh u joojin colaaddan, jiilal dambe ayaa la wareegi doona colaad aanay iyagu bilaabin, mana dhaxli doonaan wax ka badan nacayb, cabsi iyo kala fogaansho. Xalka dhabta ahi waa in la fahmo in cadowgu uusan ahayn walaalka kula nool, balse uu yahay kan ka macaasha dhiiggaaga, oo ay dhibayso nabaddaadu.

Kafkasya, dünyanın en ilginç bölgelerinden biridir. Eşsiz doğal koşulları, Avru pa ile Doğu arasındaki ilişkiler sisteminde olağanüstü stratejik önemi, yüzlerce mille te ev sahipliği yapması, gerçekten dünyanın eşsiz bir köşesidir. Kafkasya çalışmaları nın muazzam bilimsel potansiyeli uzun zamandır tarihçilerin, arkeologların, etnograf ların, gezginlerin ve diğer birçok uzmanın dikkatini çekmiştir. Yaklaşık 500 yıldır yo ğun bir şekilde devam eden bu dağlık ülkenin çalışması, büyük miktarda olgusal ma teryal biriktirmeyi mümkün kılmıştır. Dünyadaki birçok müze, Kafkas koleksiyonla rına sahip olmaktan gurur duyar. Bireysel halkların yaşamı, arkeolojik anıtların ince lenmesi hakkında yeterince özel literatür yazılmıştır. Bununla birlikte, bu dağlık ülke nin tarihi çok yönlü ve karmaşıktır ve bize Kafkasya'nın bereketli topraklarının yüzyıllar boyunca özenle koruduğu ve taşıdığı şeyin binde birinin incelendiğini hatırlatır.

Dilsel yapı açısından, Kafkas dilleri, dünyanın bu bölgesinde bulunan diğer  tüm dillerden keskin bir şekilde farklıdır ve doğrudan akrabalık olmamasına rağmen, aralarında bir Kafkas dil birliğinden bahsetmeyi gerekli kılan bazı benzerlikler var dır. Karakteristik özellikleri, ünlü sisteminin göreceli basitliği (Ubykh'te sadece iki tane var, bu bir dünya rekoru) ve ünsüzlerin olağanüstü çeşitliliğidir; yaygın ergatif cümle yapısı.

M.Ö. III-II bin yıllarda, Kafkasça konuşan kabileler sadece Kafkasya, modern Dağıstan ve Transkafkasya'da değil, aynı zamanda Mezopotamya, Batı ve Küçük Asya, Ege, Balkan ve hatta Apenin Yarımadaları'nda da yaşıyordu. Tüm bu bölgelerin en es ki nüfusunun akrabalığı, antropolojik verilerinin (Akdeniz ve Hazar alt ırkları), kültür lerinin (Kura-Araks) ve ortak dil bağlarının birliğinde izlenebilir. Sadece akrabaları nın toprakları içinde göç ettiklerini ve neredeyse bu bölgenin dışına göç etmediklerini de hesaba katarsak, o zaman etnik yakınlıkları, toprak, antropoloji, kültür ve dil ortak lığından yola çıkarak kanıtlanmış sayılabilir. 

Küçük Asya ve Batı Asya'nın en eski halkları ve dilleri ile modern Dağıstan halk ları ve dilleri, çeşitlilikleri ile karakterize edilir. Bu halkların en büyükleri Pelasglar (M.Ö. III-II bin yıl, Balkanlar), Hattiler (M.Ö. III binyıl, Küçük Asya), Hurriler (M.Ö. III-II bin yıl, Mezopotamya), Urartular (M.Ö. I. bin yıl, modern Ermenistan) ve Kaf kas Albanlarıdır (M.Ö. Tarihçilere göre, Pelasg lar ıssız Balkan Yarımadası'na yerleştiler ve arkeolojik verilere göre, insan ilk olarak Girit'te Neolitik Çağ'da M.Ö. VII. binyıl civarında ortaya çıktı. Pelasgların atası Pelas ga hakkında bilgi, en eski mitlerin bir parçasıdır:

Pelasgus, insanlara nasıl kulübe inşa edileceğini ve domuz derisi giyinmeyi gös terdi. Ayrıca Arcadia sakinlerine meşe palamudu yemeyi ve daha sonra toprağı sürme yi ve tahıl yetiştirmeyi öğretti, bu da bizi en uzak antik çağların efsaneleri dünyasına götürüyor.
M.Ö. VIII-VII binyıldan itibaren, Küçük Asya'nın güneybatısında, geleneksel olarak Çatal-Höyük olarak adlandırılan bir tarım kültürü gelişmeye başladı. Bu kül tür, Küçük Asya'nın güneyi boyunca geniş bir şerit halinde yayıldı ve muhtemelen o dönemde Rodos adası bölgesinde Ege Denizi'ne ulaştı. O zaman için şaşırtıcı derece de yüksek düzeyde tarım, el sanatları ve kültür gelişimi ile ayırt edildi. Yeterli güvenilirlikle kurulduğu için, M.Ö. 5. binyıldan itibaren, Küçük Asya topraklarında Hatto-Hurit dilleri olarak adlandırılan kabileler yaşıyordu. Bir süre sonra, Küçük Asya'ya ek olarak, Ermeni Yaylaları ve Yukarı Mezopotamya, Transkafkasya, tüm Kuzey Kafkas ya ve Hazar Denizi'nin batı kıyıları da dahil olmak üzere önemli bir bölgeyi işgal etti ler.
